articles.title: Chelsea: Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter to sell stakes in Premier League club
articles.summary: Chelsea majority owners Clearlake Capital own 61.5 per cent of club; Todd Boehly and Mark Walter own 12.8 per cent, but pair have held talks over selling shares to Clearlake, who are led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose Feliciano; Boehly was face of consortium which bought club four years ago
articles.body:
The deal paves the way for Clearlake to take full control of Chelsea, owning 86.5 per cent of the club, with Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss owning 13.5 per cent.

Boehly was the face of the consortium which bought Chelsea in 2022 but Clearlake co-founder Behdad Eghbali has become the most powerful figure at the club. Chelsea say there will be no changes to the day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the club following this transaction.

Boehly and Walter are making a small profit on their investment. Jonathan Goldstein has also stepped down from the Chelsea board, along with Boehly and Walter. They no longer have any role in Chelsea's governance, management or decision making.

There are no plans to appoint a new chairman but the executive sporting and commercial team are remaining in place.

Roman Abramovich was forced to sell Chelsea by the UK government for £2.5bn plus the guarantee of £1.5bn being invested in the club.

Boehly said: "It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club. I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

"I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the club.

"I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake's leadership."

Eghbali and Jose Feliciano , co-founders of Clearlake Capital, said in a statement: "Todd has been an important partner throughout our ownership of Chelsea, and we thank him for his time and contribution as chairman. He will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family.

"Clearlake has served as Chelsea's majority owner since 2022, and as we move to full control our focus is to continue investing in the club's infrastructure, sporting performance, player development and delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the club's supporters."

In March 2025, Boehly said Chelsea's owners could go their separate ways if they could not agree on the future of Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea bosses are considering whether to leave Stamford Bridge or to expand, with Earl's Court seen as a possible new location.

All options are being evaluated, with the project said to be complicated by the limited space in London to build.

In an interview with Bloomberg , Boehly said: "We have to think long term about what we're trying to accomplish.

"We have a big stadium development opportunity that we have to flesh out. That's going to be where we're either aligned, or we ultimately decide to go different ways."

There had been tensions too between Boehly and Clearlake in 2024.

Sky Sports News reported in September 2024 that Boehly had been unhappy with the way the club is being run and that he did not want Mauricio Pochettino to lose his job as head coach in May of that year.

Enzo Maresca replaced Pochettino and went on to win the Conference League and Club World Cup, but he left at the start of 2026, with Chelsea eventually finishing 10th and without European football.

Xabi Alonso was appointed as the new manager this summer and has the full support of the ownership.

articles.title: Sam Leavitt Injury Update, Latest on LSU QB Ahead of Ole Miss' Revenge Game vs. Lane Kiffin
articles.summary: LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt was listed on Wednesday's SEC injury report as doubtful for the No. 7 Tigers' game against No. 8 Ole Miss on Saturday, per ESPN's Pete Thamel.
articles.body:
LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt was listed on Wednesday's SEC injury report as doubtful for the No. 7 Tigers' game against No. 8 Ole Miss on Saturday, per ESPN's Pete Thamel.

Leavitt is dealing with a sore throwing shoulder, according to On3.com's Pete Nakos .

CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz also reported that the signal-caller didn't throw at practice on Wednesday.

The upcoming SEC matchup carries additional intrigue in 2026, as LSU head coach Lane Kiffin is set to travel to Vaught-Hemingway Stadium for the first time since leaving Ole Miss to become head coach of the Tigers during the 2025 season.

The Rebels opened their 2025 campaign with an 11-1 record under Kiffin and were headed towards a College Football Playoff appearance, although he departed the school to sign a seven-year contract worth $91 million with LSU.

Pete Golding took over at Ole Miss following Kiffin's exit, ending the season with a 13-2 record while advancing to the CFP semifinals.

Both schools have started this year at 2-0.

Leavitt has appeared in each of LSU's first two games, completing 62.1 percent of his throws for 574 yards and two touchdowns while getting picked off four times. He's also rushed for 135 yards and five scores, averaging 5.9 yards per attempt.

If Leavitt isn't able to play on Saturday, Landen Clark and Husan Longstreet are candidates to start under center for Kiffin's program.

Clark made brief appearances in both of LSU's games this season after transferring from Elon, finishing 7-of-10 for 109 yards and one touchdown. As for Longstreet, he's a redshirt freshman who transferred to the Tigers from USC.

Regardless of LSU's starting quarterback, the Tigers will look to find success against an Ole Miss secondary that has struggled to begin the year. The Rebels own the second-worst pass defense in the SEC by allowing 243 yards per game through the air.

Kickoff between LSU and Ole Miss on Saturday is at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Bill Belichick says speculation about Jordon Hudson's significant involvement with UNC football was 'ridiculous'
articles.summary: Both Belichick and the school have said that Hudson has no role within the football program.
articles.body:
Bill Belichick is again saying that girlfriend Jordon Hudson has had no role with North Carolina 's football program.

In an interview with the Wall Street Journal, Belichick said that he had initially asked for Hudson to be copied on his North Carolina emails shortly after he was hired because he was so busy at the start of his new job. Hudson's potential role with UNC football became the source of fascination after public records requests had unearthed Belichick's email.

In the story published Wednesday ahead of UNC's game at Clemson on Saturday, Belichick brushed off speculation of Hudson's deep involvement with the football program as "ridiculous."

"When I took the job here, it was December, and at that time I was doing five TV shows, the radio show, I had a book coming out," Belichick said. "I had a lot of other things going on when I took the job." "So," he continued, "I sent an email when I got here and I said, Can you please forward any requests to Jordon about my personal appearances so that I can work and coordinate them outside the university? Didn't have anything to do with the university. Well, that was leaked as released as 'Jordon's involved in every single thing that I do and she's copied on every email.' That's just a flat-out lie."

Belichick went on to say that he and Hudson still have a working relationship but it's "not North Carolina stuff." The school has previously said she does not have a role with the football program. So has Belichick.

Hudson rose to prominence after Belichick was hired at North Carolina following an April 2025 interview with "CBS Sunday Morning. " In it, Hudson chimed in to say that Belichick would not be answering a question about their relationship. Two weeks later, North Carolina even released a statement saying Hudson was still welcome at the team facilities — and definitely not an employee of the school — after a podcast report citing two sources that said Hudson had been told not to be at UNC's football facilities.

Recently, the off-field attention on Belichick's program has been about something much more serious. North Carolina general manager Michael Lombardi, a longtime confidant of Belichick, resigned earlier in the month amid a school investigation.

Lombardi had been placed on leave pending an investigation following a complaint from a former staffer. That investigation has now reportedly been rolled into a bigger investigation that is looking into multiple aspects in the football program, reportedly including questions surrounding allegations of drug use by defensive coordinator Steve Belichick and questions about an allegation of a sexual relationship between a recruiting staffer and a player.

Steve Belichick, Bill's son, is currently on medical leave. He came to North Carolina after his father was hired after a season as Washington's defensive coordinator.

articles.title: Messi mete su gol 100 con el Inter Miami y gana la Campeones Cup para sumar su histórico título 48
articles.standfirst: "100 goles de rosa y negro. Incontables momentos que nunca olvidaremos"
articles.summary: "100 goles de rosa y negro. Incontables momentos que nunca olvidaremos"
articles.body: Leo Messi y siempre Messi. Pasan los entrenadores por el banquillo del Inter Miami, pero la fórmula del éxito es la misma: que Lionel Messi esté de dulce. Esta vez fue el turno de Cristian 'Kily' González de saborear la gloria en su estreno, en el que el astro argentino firmó un gol y una asistencia para conquistar con un 2-0 ante Cruz Azul el torneo de la Campeones Cup (partido que enfrenta al actual ganador de la MLS con el vencedor del Campeón de Campeones de la Liga MX). Con este trofeo Leo Messi (39 años) suma 48 títulos en su carrera, confirmándose como el futbolista con más títulos entre clubes y selección. El legendario delantero argentino ha levantado 48 trofeos en sus 23 temporadas como profesional, una cifra que le sitúa como el jugador más laureado de la historia de este deporte. F.C. Barcelona (35 títulos) 10 Ligas de España, 7 Copas del Rey, 8 Supercopas de España, 4 UEFA Champions League, 3 Supercopas de Europa y 3 Mundiales de Clubes. Selección Argentina (6 títulos) 1 Copa Mundial de la FIFA (Qatar 2022), 2 Copas América (2021 y 2024), 1 Finalissima (2022), 1 Oro Olímpico (Pekín 2008) y 1 Mundial Sub-20 (2005). Inter Miami CF (4 títulos) 1 Leagues Cup (2023), 1 Supporters' Shield (2024), 1 MLS Cup (2025) y 1 Campeones Cup (2026). Paris Saint-Germain (3 títulos) 2 Ligue 1 y 1 Supercopa de Francia. Messi adelantó a su equipo en el minuto 24 con un remate de cabeza desde dentro del área pequeña a centro del uruguayo Luis Suárez, y acercó al Inter Miami al primer título de la temporada. Es el primer título de la temporada para Inter Miami y el cuarto de Messi con la camiseta rosa. Sin embargo, todavía falta el más importante: la Copa de Campeones de la Concacaf, donde el equipo de Miami suma decepción tras decepción. Este miércoles, no obstante, dio un aliento gigante a su moral tras derrotar a Cruz Azul mexicano, que llegó a la Campeones Cup como ganador del Clausura de la Liga MX y del Campeón de Campeones. Un gol de Messi en la primera mitad, el número 100 con la camiseta del Inter Miami, y otro del mediocentro brasileño Casemiro a falta de diez minutos, a saque de esquina ejecutado por el argentino, sellaron el triunfo y firmaron el debut soñado del 'Kily' González. Los primeros minutos fueron de mayor control de Cruz Azul, pero sin peligro más allá de dos disparos desde el interior del área que el guardameta del Inter Miami paró sin gran dificultad. El conjunto mexicano dominaba el balón y los locales no lograban entrar en el partido, ante lo que Messi decidió caer a la banda derecha. Sin embargo, no lo hizo en busca de nuevos espacios, sino para charlar casi medio minuto con González y encontrar soluciones. Secretos al margen sobre lo conversado, lo cierto es que el Inter Miami se adelantó casi de inmediato. Fue Messi, ¿quién si no?, el que inauguró la era González con el que fue su tanto número 100 con 'Las Garzas'. El astro argentino llegó desde atrás para rematar de cabeza dentro del área pequeña un centro de Suárez desde la derecha y anotó el único tanto de una primera mitad sin mucha historia. Solo otra combinación entre los dos 'ex' del Barcelona estuvo a punto de cambiar el marcador, pero Willer Ditta estuvo atento para sacar entre los palos una vaselina del uruguayo a pase de Messi. Mientras, Jordi Alba, socio habitual de ambos que se retiró el año pasado en las filas del Inter Miami, seguía el partido desde la grada. Los cambios que introdujo Huiqui al descanso, quitando a Jesús Orozco y a Carlos Rotondi, buscaron consolidar la banda izquierda de Cruz Azul. No obstante, las arrancadas de Messi continuaron siendo el principal estímulo de una grada mucho más vacía de lo que se espera de un partido por un título, y repleta de camisetas del Cruz Azul. En una de esas jugadas el argentino anotó, pero el banderín del asistente anuló la jugada. Poco después, un esprint de los de antaño dejó atrás a dos rivales, pero el tercero le quitó el balón cuando ya se intuía un tanto memorable. Una nueva ronda de cambios pareció despertar definitivamente al conjunto mexicano a la hora de partido, cuando un remate de Gabriel Fernández a centro de Alan Mozo -ambos recién ingresados desde el banqullo- acabó con el balón estrellándose en el palo. Ahí fue donde jugó un papel estelar Casemiro, el fichaje de lujo del Inter Miami en el último verano, sacando por alto cada balón centrado por los jugadores de Cruz Azul. El brasileño, que destacó a su llegada la felicidad que le brindaba compartir vestuario con Messi, culminó su actuación con el tanto que selló el triunfo del Inter Miami, empujando a la red un balón de córner lanzado por el argentino a menos de diez minutos para el final. La fiesta fue completa en Miami, que volvió a celebrar un título, y se brindó una alegría en medio de un año duro a nivel de resultados, que solo resolvería la segunda MLS Cup consecutiva. La Campeones Cup es el cuarto título de Messi con la camiseta rosa, tras la Leagues Cup 2023, el Supporters' Shield 2024 y la MLS Cup 2025. Curiosamente Messi inauguró su cuenta goleadora con Inter Miami precisamente contra el Cruz Azul en su debut en julio de 2023. "100 goles de rosa y negro. Incontables momentos que nunca olvidaremos", compartió el Inter Miami. 2. Inter Miami: Dayne St.Clair; Facundo Mura (Gonzalo Luján m.77), Casemiro, Fricio Caicedo (Micael, m.70); Rodrigo De Paul, Yannick Bright, Matías Galarza (Alexander Shaw, m.62); Lionel Messi, Luis Suárez y Germán Berterame (Sergio Reguilón, m.70). Entrenador: Cristian González. 0. Cruz Azul: Kevin Mier; Jeremy Márquez (Alan Mozo, m.63), Willer Ditta, Amaury García (Christian Ebere, m.80), Jesús Orozco (Gonzalo Piovi, m.46), Carlos Rotondi (Omar Campos, m.46); José Paradela, Erik Lira (Gabriel Fernández, m.63), Agustín Palavecino, Carlos Rodríguez, Gabriel Fernández y Nicolás Ibáñez. Entrenador: Joel Huiqui. Goles: 1-0, m.24: Lionel Messi. 2-0, m.81: Casemiro. Árbitro: Keylor Herrera, de Costa Rica. Amonestó a Matías Galarza y a Alexander Shaw, del Inter Miami, y a Willer Ditta y Gabriel Fernández, del Cruz Azul. Incidencias: Partido de la final de la Campeones Cup jugado en el Nu Stadium de Miami (Florida).

articles.title: Un aviso para lanzarse al derbi
articles.standfirst: El Atlético exhibe su poderío antes de recibir al Real Madrid el próximo domingo
articles.summary: El Atlético exhibe su poderío antes de recibir al Real Madrid el próximo domingo
articles.body: Pese a que Simeone viene insistiendo en que este Atlético aún está en construcción y que muchos de sus jugadores aún tratan de alcanzar su mejor nivel después de que su presencia en el Mundial o su incorporación tardía al club les impidiera hacer una pretemporada al uso, lo cierto es que sus jugadores, a cuatro días de medirse a su eterno rival, ya han firmado su actuación más redonda. Una exhibición de poderío en toda regla. Porque fueron cuatro tantos, pero por merecimientos y acumulación de llegadas, la goleada pudo ser mucho más abultada. Del mismo modo que tras tres salidas (Sevilla, Bilbao y Liverpool) recibiendo goles, Oblak encadena su segunda presencia consecutiva con la portería a cero. Mejor imposible en vísperas de afrontar un derbi que también empezaría a jugarse desde la grada. El Atlético se presenta lanzado. “Siempre el derbi es especial y más jugarlo en casa. Es nuestro rival de la ciudad y queremos ganarle, pero tenemos que hacer muy bien las cosas porque son un gran equipo. Ojalá podamos ganarlo y darle una alegría a la gente”, afirmaría Koke. “Estamos muy contentos de ganar, sabíamos que en la vuelta a casa después de partidos difíciles era clave ganar y más antes del derbi. Estamos muy contentos”, secundaría Kang-in Lee para dejar patentes las sensaciones que imperan en el vestuario antes de recibir al Real Madrid. Una inyección de moral que viene acompañada de un refuerzo en el estado físico, pues además de las rotaciones dispuestas por Simeone con el once (Pubill o Hancko esperarían en el banquillo), la goleada permitiría también resguardar a otros como el Cuti Romero o Lookman... para una cita en la que todas las fuerzas serán pocas.

articles.title: Con 9... y los falsos puntas
articles.standfirst: Kang-in y Baena también marcan tras la ‘presentación’ de Jonathan David
articles.summary: Kang-in y Baena también marcan tras la ‘presentación’ de Jonathan David
articles.body: Con un 9 como Jonathan David, primero, y con dos falsos puntas como Kang-in y Baena, después. Tras un auténtico tiroteo de 27 remates sobre la portería de Aitor Fernández incomensurable, el Atlético demostró que tiene pólvora, y sobre todo, vías para llegar al gol de todos los colores. Era la primera vez que Simeone salía de inicio con un especialista en LaLiga (Julián Alvarez sí fue titular en Champions), pero tanto su plan A como el B salió a las mil maravillas gracias al gran juego desplegado antes de llegar el momento de culminarlo en el área. Por eso respondió el canadiense y por eso redondearon la fiesta los dos talentosos futbolistas que ocuparon el frente del ataque tras su salida. Hasta el punto de que los tres goleadores al margen de Le Normand pudieron acabar con una cuenta aún mayor. Así, antes y después de que Jonathan David abriera la lata y se reivindicara como una opción de plenas garantías para suplir la ausencia de La Araña y Sorloth, tanto él como Kang-in y Baena coleccionarían innumerables ocasiones que no se tradujeron en gol por falta de puntería o por las grandes intervenciones del portero. La producción sería la misma con un hombre de referencia como el canadiense que con los dos genios bajitos como delanteros mentirosos. “Los jugadores atacantes intentamos hacer nuestro trabajo. En la primera parte nos costó finalizar, pero estamos contentos por la victoria. Lo importante es trabajar fuerte y mejorar”, resumiría Kang-in.

articles.title: Laporta: "Casablanca y Madrid son lo mismo, la final del Mundial 2030 debería ser en el Camp Nou"
articles.standfirst: Joan Laporta comparte que "hemos propuesto" el Spotify Camp Nou como sede de la final del Mundial 2030
articles.summary: Joan Laporta comparte que "hemos propuesto" el Spotify Camp Nou como sede de la final del Mundial 2030
articles.body: Joan Laporta, presidente del F.C. Barcelona, postuló al Spotify Camp Nou para ser la sede de la final del Mundial 2030 por delante de Casablanca y Madrid. "Casablanca y Madrid son lo mismo", bromeó el presidente culé haciendo un juego de palabras (entre Casablanca y la Casa Blanca en referencia al Real Madrid). Laporta defendió en el programa 'Què T'hi Jugues' de la Cadena SER que "la final del Mundial no debería ser ni en Casablanca ni en Madrid, debería ser en el Spotify Camp Nou". "Lo digo por una razón. 105.000 espectadores. Yo creo que esto la FIFA lo tendrá en cuenta. Y además... ya se organizó una final del Mundial en el Santiago Bernabéu en 1982". Laporta compartió que "con todos los respetos a Marruecos, la final del Mundial 2030 se debería jugar en el estado español, y además España es una selección que campeona del mundo". "La final del Mundial 2030 en el Spotify Camp Nou sería un reconocimiento internacional que nosotros queremos tener y así lo propondremos. Argumentaremos estas razones y otras que seguro que se nos ocurrirán", subrayó.

articles.title: El drama familiar de Nacho Novo: "Nuestro hermoso chico ha fallecido trágicamente"
articles.standfirst: Por el momento la familia no ha querido hacer pública la causa de su fallecimiento
articles.summary: Por el momento la familia no ha querido hacer pública la causa de su fallecimiento
articles.body: Nacho Novo, exfutbolista español de 47 años y actual entrenador del Darvel FC de Escocia, confirmó la muerte de su hijastro Ross con 26 años. "Nada en mi vida podría haberme preparado para escribir este mensaje. Estamos completamente destrozados al compartir la triste noticia de que nuestro precioso chico ha fallecido trágicamente" publicó en sus redes sociales el ferrolano, ex jugador de Racing Ferrol, Somozas, Huesca, Raith Rovers, Dundee, Glasgow Rangers, Sporting Gijón, Legia Varsovia, Greenock Morton, Carlisle United, Carolina Railhawks y Glentoran. Ross era hijo de Donna Clark, la ex esposa del exfutbolista gallego (se casaron en 2015). Nacho Novo, que se refería a Ross como "mi hijo", mantenían una estrella relación a pesar de separación matrimonial. "Descansa en paz, hermano mayor. Te voy a echar mucho de menos. Espero que estés bien y a salvo allá arriba. Gracias por cuidarme siempre. Te quiero muchísimo; no puedo creer que esto sea verdad. Fuiste el mejor hermano del mundo. Eternos 26 años", publicó en TikTok el hermano de 16 años de Ross. Por el momento la familia no ha querido hacer pública la causa de su fallecimiento. En su etapa en Escocia el español Nacho Novo ganó tres títulos de la Premier League escocesa, dos Copas de Escocia y tres Copas de la Liga y se convirtió en uno de los jugadores más populares del histórico Rangers FC. El Darvel Football Club, equipo que entrena Nacho Novo, publicó que "estamos devastados por la trágica noticia del fallecimiento del hijo de nuestro entrenador, Nacho Novo, Ross, a la temprana edad de 26 años". Michael Mols, exjugador del Ranger, ofreció sus condolencias y oraciones: "Increíble, Nacho. Mis pensamientos, oraciones y condolencias". Steven Davis, también ex del Ranger, publicó: "Mis pensamientos están con todos vosotros en este momento tan difícil". La comentarista deportiva Laura Woods escribió: "Siento muchísimo tu pérdida, Nacho; que tu hermoso hijo descanse en paz". La estrella de la lucha libre Grado compartió: "Siento mucho escuchar esto, Nacho; es algo absolutamente desgarrador. Mis pensamientos están contigo y con tu familia".

articles.title: El Atleti se carga de fe para el derbi
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', por Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', por Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Partido en horario raro en el Metropolitano, siete de la tarde entre semana, a pesar de lo cual hubo una gran entrada. Como ya se ventea el derbi, el macizo de la afición atlética acudió en busca de argumentos para encararlo con optimismo y el Cholo se los ofreció en cantidad. Dio unos cuantos descansos y el equipo no se resintió en lo más mínimo. Fue un flujo de ataque continuo, no sólo hasta el primer gol, sino también tras él, y tras el 2-0, el 3-0, el 4-0… La goleada llegó sin la menor culpa, sino lo contrario, de Aitor Fernández, que hizo media docena de paradas imponentes justificando la decisión de Ramis de hacer el relevo en la portería. A falta de Sorloth y Julián Alvarez, el Atlético ha encontrado en el canadiense Jonathan David un delantero centro válido. Ayer volvió a marcar. Se mueve bien en la brecha, es un insistente rematador y tiene puntería. También está muy bien Kang-in Lee por la derecha, y Lookman, una vez recuperado su sitio en la izquierda, vuelve a ser peligroso. Con las incorporaciones de los laterales, Llorente y Grimaldo, el talento siempre amenazante de Baena y algunos buenos pases profundos de Johnny Cardoso, el Atlético hizo las delicias de la afición. Por atrás no tuvo problemas, y el único que tuvo se lo resolvió el árbitro mandando al limbo el gol osasunista, él sabrá por qué. Pero el equipo madrileño fue tan superior y remató tanto que no cabe tener eso en cuenta. Juego constante de ataque, eso es lo que la afición va demandando al Cholo. ¿Lo hará así el domingo? Es evidente que jugarán algunos de los que ayer sólo entraron al final, entre ellos Giuliano. Y es probable que se afirme con tres centrales, de modo que por delante no será lo mismo. Ya veremos. En cualquier caso, queda ahí esa buena impresión, bastante alejada de la que dejó el Madrid en Elche, donde ganó por los pelos y regresó metido en lenguas por la actitud de Vinicius, Mbappé y Konaté, un tema feo, incómodo y resbaladizo donde los haya.

articles.title: Espaldarazo para Messi en la carrera por el Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: Kily González asegura que "Messi debe ganar el Balón de Oro" con 39 años y lo argumenta
articles.summary: Kily González asegura que "Messi debe ganar el Balón de Oro" con 39 años y lo argumenta
articles.body: El nuevo entrenador del Inter Miami, Cristian 'Kily' González, aseguró que Lionel Messi le dijo que le iba a ayudar a conquistar la Campeones Cup en su debut como técnico de 'Las Garzas', y "lo cumplió" con un gol y una asistencia. "Messi me dijo que me iba a hacer salir campeón y lo cumplió. Defensivamente estuvimos muy bien. No tengo palabras de lo que estoy sintiendo. Es alegría, felicidad, tantas emociones juntas", dijo González en la conferencia de prensa posterior al partido que ganaron por 2-0 a Cruz Azul. La victoria pone fin a una racha de tres partidos seguidos sin ganar y brinda una alegría para un equipo llamado a dominar el continente, pero que estaba cerca de sufrir un año en blanco tras caer en la Copa de Campeones de la Concacaf y en la Leagues Cup. Por lo que González destacó que supone un "envión anímico" para la plantilla, que actualmente ocupa la segunda posición de la Conferencia Este de la MLS, a 9 puntos del líder. Sobre el partido ante Cruz Azul, el técnico destacó el hambre de su equipo, repleto de jugadores "que han ganado tanto" y que aún así salieron con el ansia de llevar un nuevo título a las vitrinas del Inter Miami. Destacó especialmente a Messi (39 años), al que describió como "el número uno", y defendió que se merece el Balón de Oro. "No hay otro como él; no tengo ninguna duda que el Balón (de Oro) le tiene que tocar a él. Con la edad que tiene, el Mundial que hizo, lo que representa para todos, no sólo en lo futbolístico sino también en los valores de vida...debería ser justo que se lo lleve él", subrayó. González fue anunciado a finales de agosto como nuevo entrenador del Inter Miami en reemplazo de Guillermo Hoyos, pero no pudo debutar hasta este miércoles por problemas con su permiso de trabajo. Su última experiencia en los banquillos databa del pasado octubre, cuando finalizó su vinculación con el Platense argentino. El Inter Miami nunca había conquistado la Campeones Cup, un torneo que disputó como vigente campeón de la MLS Cup, un título que alzó el pasado diciembre por primera vez en su corta historia.

articles.body: Manchester United’s difficult start to the season took another turn for the worse on Wednesday as they surrendered a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 to Brighton and exit the English League Cup.United looked in control early at Old Trafford, racing into a 2-0 lead within the opening 10 minutes. Academy graduate Shea Lacey scored in the eighth minute on his first senior start, before Mason Mount doubled the advantage just two minutes later.But Brighton fought back and turned the game around after the break. articles.title: Israel's Under-20 footballers and a golden generation of hope and talent
articles.summary: Can the potential of a golden generation of Israel's footballers, in sport and society, be realised?
articles.body:
It was, says Ido Rakovsky, like reporting on "science fiction", rather than sport.

Israel, whose senior team have qualified for the World Cup just once, had beaten global powerhouses Brazil in the quarter-finals of the under-20 version of the tournament.

At the final whistle, the commentator covering the match for Israeli television vowed "you will tell of this night to your children, and they will tell it to your grandchildren".

Five days later, the team's semi-final against Uruguay was the most-watched thing of the evening on Israeli television, drawing a 23% viewing share.

Politicians clamoured to congratulate the team.

"That summer, everybody was watching under-20 football, everybody knew the players," says Rakovsky, who was covering the team for Israeli media outlet Haaretz.

"Everybody in Israel fell in love with these kids."

It wasn't just their deeds on the pitch that felt otherworldly, though.

After scoring a stoppage-time winner against Uzbekistan in the last 16, Anan Khalaili had given an interview to Israeli television.

In it Khalaili, an Israeli Arab, thanked the viewers back home for staying up late to watch his team win in Argentina.

To do so, he used the words 'Am Yisrael' - a Hebrew phrase that means 'People of Israel' and is bound up in Jewish religion, community, culture and history.

"That an Arab player used that figure of speech said something about the identity of that team," says Rakovsky.

"That team made real the claim that football can really bring people together - that Muslim players are part of the national team of the Jewish state, representing Israel and creating something better, both for the present and future."

But a little over four months after Khalaili's interview and the win over Brazil, Hamas attacked Israel.

The armed Palestinian group killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostages. In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza. The United Nations believes the retaliation has killed more than 70,000 Palestinians. , external

As the war goes on, can the potential of a golden generation of Israel's footballers, in sport and society, be realised?

Beaten 1-0 by eventual champions Uruguay, Israel finished third at that Under-20 World Cup in 2023.

The same set of players, with a few additions and omissions, had already impressed at continental level.

They were runners-up at 2022's Under-19 Euros, beaten by England in extra-time in the final, and would go on to make the semi-finals of 2023's Under-20 Euros.

Israel has produced outstanding players in the past. Eyal Berkovic and Yossi Benayoun were technical, gifted attackers with long Premier League careers.

But a depth of talent, emerging together, sets the current cohort apart.

Khalaili has been one of the most sought-after young prospects in Europe this summer.

After his £21.5m move to Inter Milan fell through, Crystal Palace saw off competition from Nottingham Forest to pick him up for a similar fee from Belgian side Union Saint-Gilloise.

Playmaker Oscar Gloukh, 22, wears Ajax's number 10 shirt after his form earned a move from Red Bull Salzburg.

Left-back Roy Revivo signed for Spanish club Elche on transfer deadline day this month from Maccabi Tel Aviv, while Twente defender Stav Lemkin, also 23, is also highly rated.

Dor Turgeman, Ilay Feingold and Idan Toklomati are impressing in Major League Soccer in the United States.

All have now won full caps, but were moulded into a collective, cohesive unit - something that has often been beyond the senior side - by Israel's age-grade coach Ofir Haim.

"It isn't an issue at all here," Haim said , external of the different backgrounds in his squad during the 2023 Under-20 World Cup.

"We don't have any problem with religion. Not at all. We have players here who put on tefillin [Jewish ceremonial wear, containing verses from the Torah] - and Anan [Khalaili], Hamza [Shibli] and Ahmed [Salman] perform the Muslim prayers.

"We don't even talk about this. We unite everybody, and I wish the country were as united as this team."

Football has long been the part of Israeli society where communities mix together who may not otherwise meet.

"The majority of the Jewish people who arrived in the mandate period [a spell between 1923 and 1948 where the region was run by Britain] emigrated from Europe," says Dr Omer Einav, a historian and author of Defending the Goal, a book on Israel's football history.

"They were Europeans and when you think about cinema, music, theatre, dance, they had nothing in common with Middle Eastern culture. Nothing, except football. That was the only common language, the only thing they both love in the same way."

Encouraged by the British administrators who ran the region, teams from different communities, and some made up of elements of each, would play against each other.

When the modern state of Israel was formed in 1948, much of the Arab population that remained inside its borders continued to identify as or with Palestinians. Most still do.

They are also an intrinsic part of Israeli football.

While they make up 20% of Israel's population, they represent about 35% of those involved in the sport at elite level nationally.

The first Arab player to represent Israel's national team was Rifaat Turk in 1976. In 2018, Bibars Natcho became the first Muslim to captain the team.

Turk was roundly abused. Natcho's decision not to sing Israel's national anthem, the lyrics of which relate to the Jewish search for a homeland, was condemned by some. , external

For a short time in the summer of 2023, it seemed as if Haim's under-20 side might offer a watershed moment of unity and co-existence.

But football, like everything in Israel, changed on 7 October.

Matan Segal directed Kick It Out Israel, an anti-discrimination initiative with similar aims but no link to the English organisation of the same name, for almost four years before stepping down a few months ago.

Racism has long been present in Israeli club football. Beitar Jerusalem's fans are among the most notorious.

The most extreme Beitar fans have long taunted Israeli Arabs with chants of "may your village burn", while declaring themselves "forever pure".

However during his time at Kick It Out Israel, Segal saw racism against Arab players become more virulent and widespread.

Covid, during which fans radicalised online during lockdown, was one cause.

The election of Israel's far-right government at the end of 2022, legitimising views towards Palestinians that were previously seen as extreme, was a second.

"Before 7 October, people generally respected the Arab players," Segal said.

"Even though they had difficulties with them not singing the Israeli anthem, they respected them and they could talk about it.

"After 7 October though, we saw an increase in racist remarks.

"It was happening at small clubs where we hadn't seen it before. There were terrible songs - 'Let's kill all Arabs', 'There are no schools in Gaza because there are no children left'."

Football, inevitably, has become a focal point for emotion generated by the conflict.

Clubs which are usually bitter rivals came together to remember those killed by Hamas. Scarves were part of the commemoration at the site of the Nova music festival, where hundreds were killed.

Hapoel Jerusalem's club badge now features a silhouette of Hersh Goldberg-Polin, who was abducted and killed in captivity and whose parents have campaigned for peace through their grief.

Meanwhile, Israeli Defence Force (IDF) soldiers have posed with club flags and banners while on operation in Gaza, dedicating their actions to the clubs and ultras back home. , external

In such a heightened atmosphere, young footballers – closely connected to the conflict through Israel's programme of national service and a barrage of online commentary and images – are under constant scrutiny and pressure.

Gloukh's lifelong friend Afik Tery was killed by a Hamas explosive while serving in the IDF.

After his death, Gloukh posted a poignant set of pictures , external of the pair arm-in-arm over time - as young boys at birthday parties, as young men at a wedding - with the final slide showing Tery's funeral.

Among the online replies were the taunts of pro-Palestinians.

For Israel players with Palestinian heritage, the stakes are especially and dangerously high.

Dia Saba plays in a similar playmaking role to Gloukh. The 33-year-old has scored three goals in 13 appearances for Israel.

He is unlikely ever to add to that tally.

Saba was one of Maccabi Haifa's most high-profile stars when, at the start of the conflict, his wife Narmin posted a message to Instagram.

"There are children in Gaza, too," she wrote.

Saba apologised for the outrage caused, but could not save his career in Israel. He left Maccabi Haifa in 2025 and now plays for Turkish side Amedspor.

"My dream was to play for Maccabi Haifa, the club that I support, the team that I grew up with," Saba said at the time.

"I wanted to continue. But sometimes there are reasons that are stronger than us that don't allow it."

Saba and others are used to having their loyalty questioned. From all sides.

Many in the Arab world would like more Palestinian prospects within Israel to follow the example of Ataa Jaber.

Jaber captained Israel's Under-21 side but switched nationalities , external to represent Palestine in June 2023, saying he could no longer separate sport and politics after seeing police evict Palestinian families from their homes in Israeli-occupied East Jerusalem .

Switching away from a high level of international football damaged his prospects of a move to Europe. At home, there were calls for his Israeli citizenship to be revoked. But, for Jaber, it was preferable to representing a country whose actions he deplored.

Those footballers who voice an opinion on the conflict choose their words carefully.

Beram Kayal, the former Brighton, Celtic and Israel player, knows the dilemmas and reality well.

"To be Arabic in Israel, it's sometimes hard," he says. "Sometimes it is tough.

"Opportunities-wise, sometimes we are not on the same level."

However, he believes in a pluralistic future for Israel and football as a tool to achieve it.

His friendship with Tomer Hemed - whom he first met as a young teenager at Maccabi Haifa's academy and later played alongside at Brighton and Charlton, as well as international level - sums up his approach.

"When I played with Tomer, he prayed like this," he says, touching his hand to his back of his head to indicate a kippah, the small skullcap worn as a sign of Jewish faith.

"And I was praying for Allah," he adds, raising his arms above his shoulders in worship.

"He was my team-mate and he is my brother.

"In football, on the pitch, you never look at colour, culture or religion. You just want the best people around you to win the game."

The 38-year-old is now employed by Israel's Football Association to work with young talents from Palestinian areas.

In doing so he works alongside former Israel goalkeeper Boni Ginzburg, who played across Glasgow at Rangers and is now the IFA's technical director.

After Arabic was relegated behind Hebrew as Israel's official language by a controversial 2018 law promoted by prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the IFA put on Hebrew language lessons for Arabic-speaking coaches to ensure they could still obtain their qualifications.

"Not in our building," says Kayal when asked about the precedence given to Hebrew.

"I'm in this place [the IFA] to bring the culture of the Arabic people to the table.

"I say to the Arabic players when they come into the national team: Speak in your language, don't be afraid, don't be shy to speak, don't just afraid to show yourself.

"Israel is a young country. We need to learn from our DNA, to see the different between the Jewish, the Circassians, the Arabic, the Muslim, the Christian, the Druze – all the colours – put that together and learn what we could do better."

Israel's aim is to go better than their national team has managed in more than 50 years.

Ran Ben-Shimon was appointed as the senior side's head coach in 2024. He was given the goal of converting youthful promise into qualification for Euro 2028, which will be staged in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

Success would place more stress on Israel's players and, potentially, squad unity.

Large-scale protests are planned for Republic of Ireland's forthcoming Nations League matches with Israel. Dublin will host seven games at the tournament.

Villa Park in Birmingham, from which Maccabi Tel Aviv fans were banned from attending a Europa League match in November, will stage four matches.

Hampden Park, two miles across Glasgow from where Celtic fans have held vociferous pro-Palestine protests, has six.

Wherever Israel play, players will be confronted with criticism of their country's treatment of Palestinians, both at home and in Gaza, that is rarely voiced at home.

"Israelis are very sensitive to anyone showing any kind of sympathy for what happened on 7 October," says Dr Sophia Solomon, part of Ben-Gurion University's Center for Sports Diplomacy.

"It is like denying the Holocaust, that is the proportion of it. A war is a special situation, it wasn't like this before, but to express your agony became more encouraged as we saw the European arena become more anti-Israeli.

"One reaction ignited another and there is more obligation to identify yourself with the victims of 7 October."

She believes that it will take time for Israeli society, footballers included, to understand the past three years and speak openly about the conflict.

"Until the ongoing war ends, no-one can say what he thinks," she said. "Even after the Middle East returns to its 'normal' craziness, maybe it will take a decade to pass before people can start talking about their experiences and expectations.

"Time has to pass until you can touch certain areas, and at the moment you can see a lot of avoidance about talking about it, even mentioning it."

The time for this stellar generation to fulfil their potential may come before that.

It may not. Translating youth-level promise to senior-level product is never simple.

But, whatever the future holds, for a few months, in the summer of 2023, Haim and his team gave Israel something special.

"We saw Anan Khalaili and Hamza Shibli scoring against Brazil and that was our hope, that was the future. That was our future," says Einav.

"I'm not so optimistic, but people thought maybe it's really a magical thing that can help Israeli society in general.

"There was something there, something new, something where people said 'OK, if we co-operate, if we work together, we can also succeed in sport.'

"That's what we all care about, right? We want to be good at sports. We are sick of watching the World Cup from our living room.

"I think football is in some isolated, sterilised dimension - some kind of bubble - inside Israeli society. It is not hermetic. A lot of dirt comes in - racism, violence - but I do believe that football can reflect good things that can happen. The equality of chances, the tolerance and solidarity of all people living here.

"It can't heal anything but it can help us see one another in a more human way.

"So, yeah there was definitely a moment, but it was before our world changed and collapsed."

Only time will tell what remains of that moment and whether it can be revived.

articles.title: Savannah DeMelo: USA midfielder sues doctors after on-pitch heart attack
articles.summary: United States women's national team player Savannah DeMelo is suing a hospital and two doctors after she suffered a heart attack on the pitch last year.
articles.body:
United States women's national team player Savannah DeMelo is suing a hospital and two doctors after she suffered a heart attack on the pitch last year.

Midfielder DeMelo, who has seven senior caps for the USA, has filed a lawsuit against University of Louisville Health (UofL Health) for negligence.

The 28-year-old, who plays for Racing Louisville, collapsed in the first half of a National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) match on 14 September 2025.

According to documents , external seen by BBC Sport, the case was filed on Tuesday morning with Jefferson Circuit Court in Kentucky, where her club is based - a year and a day after her on-field collapse.

DeMelo's filing claims UofL Health and two doctors, Dr Sarabjeet Suri and Dr Jennifer Daily, "failed to act as a reasonably prudent and competent medical practice, and such negligence was a substantial factor in causing DeMelo to suffer severe physical injuries, including, but not limited to, her cardiac arrest."

Dr Daily, according to her online UofL biography , external , is Racing Louisville's chief medical officer. The lawsuit states DeMelo was under the care of Dr Daily from January 2024 to July 2026.

It states that in March 2025, Dr Daily referred DeMelo to Dr Suri for "evaluation and treatment" after she had been complaining of chest pain, dizziness and shortness of air; Dr Suri obtained a history, performed a physical examination and ordered diagnostic tests.

Nearly six months later, DeMelo suffered the cardiac arrest.

"She was subsequently diagnosed and treated for ventricular tachycardia [an abnormal heart rhythm]," the suit states.

DeMelo, who has spent her entire professional career with Racing Louisville, has not played since her collapse.

In a post to her Instagram page , external on Tuesday, De Melo - who was picked in the USA squad for the 2023 Women's World Cup and started their first two games - marked the anniversary of the incident.

"A year ago today, while playing soccer, I collapsed due to an undiagnosed cardiac arrhythmia, that caused me to go into cardiac arrest," she wrote.

"I respect and appreciate the privacy everyone has met me with while going through everything I have this year. I'll never be able to fully put into words how emotionally hard this year has been. There has been a lot of uncertainty and emotions intertwined with it all."

articles.title: La peña madridista de Ceuta responde a Mbappé, Vinicius y Konaté
articles.standfirst: Miguel Ángel Montano explicó en La Tribu cómo recibieron los madridistas ceutíes el gesto de los tres jugadores con la camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta: "Nos dolió bastante, y más siendo jugadores de nuestro Real Madrid"
articles.summary: Miguel Ángel Montano explicó en La Tribu cómo recibieron los madridistas ceutíes el gesto de los tres jugadores con la camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta: "Nos dolió bastante, y más siendo jugadores de nuestro Real Madrid"
articles.body: Miguel Ángel Montano, presidente de la peña madridista de Ceuta, atendió a Raúl Varela en La Tribu para explicar cómo están viviendo la situación en la ciudad y, especialmente, cómo recibieron el gesto de Mbappé, Vinicius y Konaté con la camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta antes del partido del Real Madrid ante el Elche. Montano relató que en la peña recibieron inicialmente con alegría la iniciativa del conjunto blanco. La reacción cambió, según contó, al comprobar lo sucedido con los tres futbolistas. "Estábamos viendo las imágenes en el vestuario y veíamos que llevaban la camiseta de apoyo a nuestra ciudad y todos nos pusimos súper contentos. Pero, después vimos que los tres jugadores del Real Madrid se la subían y no mostraban el mensaje. Nos quedamos como diciendo: 'Esto no es apoyarnos'. Nos dolió bastante y más siendo jugadores de nuestro Real Madrid". Montano también se refirió a las explicaciones posteriores de Mbappé y aseguró que entiende que el francés quisiera mostrar su preocupación por las personas migrantes, aunque considera que podía haberlo hecho en otro momento. "Creo que Mbappé ha dicho que él compartía nuestra situación, pero que también se ponía en el lado de la inmigración y por eso no se levantaba la camiseta", explicó. A continuación, expuso lo que él habría hecho: "Si tú tienes una camiseta de apoyo a la ciudad de Ceuta no te la quites y mañana, o al partido siguiente, saca una de apoyo a los inmigrantes. Tan sencillo como eso". Tras escuchar las explicaciones de Mbappé, Montano añadió: "A mí me parece bien que se disculpe. Es de bien nacido ser agradecido". Sin embargo, insistió en su posición: "Ayer tocaba Ceuta y mañana tocará a los inmigrantes". El presidente de la peña madridista quiso rebajar, en cambio, las críticas de quienes consideran que los tres jugadores no deberían continuar vistiendo la camiseta blanca. "Eso es ir demasiado lejos, no estarán ni bien informados de la situación", dijo sobre los que piden tomar esa decisión. Montano diferenció en todo momento la posición de esos futbolistas de la del club. "El Madrid está por encima de todo esto, dará una respuesta y nos apoyará seguro", aseguró. Para el presidente de la peña, lo ocurrido respondió a una decisión individual: "Eso ha sido una cosa de cada uno. Ha sido a nivel de estos tres jugadores, no del resto de la plantilla". Montano también explicó a La Tribu cómo vive personalmente estos días en Ceuta. "Realmente no tengo miedo, pero voy con precaución. Siempre estoy pendiente: abro mi casa o la puerta de mi garaje y miro siempre a un lado y a otro...". Pese a todo, intenta conservar su vida cotidiana. "He seguido con mi rutina diaria", explicó Montano, que lleva vinculado a la peña madridista desde 1987 y regresó a su presidencia este año. Y cuando Raúl Varela le preguntó si cambiaría una Liga o incluso otra Champions por que Ceuta recuperase la normalidad y sus habitantes pudieran vivir tranquilos, su respuesta fue inmediata: "¿Dónde hay que firmarlo? Que lo firmo ahora mismo".

articles.title: Tony Pulis column: Why dealing with defeat is the key for Lampard at Coventry
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains why Coventry boss Frank Lampard needs to manage himself as well as his players after their poor start to the season.
articles.body:
Managing a newly-promoted team in the Premier League is very demanding, as Frank Lampard is finding out at Coventry.

It's the highest level, not just for the technical ability of the players that your team faces but also the sheer physicality that these players possess, and it feels like the gap to the Championship is getting greater every season.

From my experience in the same situation, you have to be really smart in the way you approach each game and recognise the importance of preparation for each specific opponent, because your team has to be organised in possession, and definitely out of possession.

Teams in the Premier League counter-attack with greater efficiency so being solid behind your own attacking play is absolutely vital.

But the real advice I would give to managers in Frank's shoes is to manage yourself, and your own time, as well as your players.

By that I mean you have to try to stay fresh and positive, because invariably you are going to go on bad runs of defeats like Coventry are on, which can drag your mood down.

Find a way of getting everyone back on track

I can tell you now that, whoever you are playing, if you get beaten - and especially beaten heavily like Coventry were by Brighton on Sunday - then it resonates with you. It's the same for every manager.

For Frank, whether it is losing at home to Hull or Brighton , or against Arsenal and Manchester City , then it will hurt.

But it is how he deals with those defeats that will decide what happens next.

Being the leader of a group of young men, you cannot look washed out and empty on a Monday morning after a heavy loss.

Yes, inside you will be hurting and your pride will be taking a bashing but everyone at the club will be waiting for your reaction, and will act accordingly.

Walking into the training ground in a dark mood and with your head around your backside just does not work, irrespective of what you are feeling inside.

I've been in that situation many times myself as a manager and what you have to do is puff your chest out and find a way of getting everyone back on track and working even harder with a set focus on the next game.

That's what all good leaders do. It is draining at times, but that is why managing your time and prioritising the issues that you can resolve is so important.

When I took Stoke up to the Premier League in 2008, I was learning on my feet.

We did not make a great start and I had to roll my sleeves up and get on with what I'd got in my squad, and really focus on getting results.

But away from that I was always forward thinking and I was quick at recognising what was needed to improve our chances of staying up.

When the window opened again in January, we were already in discussions with Tottenham for Matty Etherington, to supply us with crosses and chances from the wing.

We needed more goals too, so I took James Beattie from Sheffield United. They were a Championship side but that didn't matter because he had a record of scoring goals in the top flight.

We have heard so much about recruiting the right players in the right positions, and it is true today as it was in my day. Both lads played a significant role in keeping us up.

Coventry haven't scored a goal yet, and people might look in from the outside and feel the forward areas are an issue for them because the usual thinking is that the centre-forward has to lead the scoring charts, or a wide player or the number 10.

But the emphasis is on everyone to chip in and I would also reinforce one of the points I made in this column last season, about the importance of defending properly too.

On average, clean sheets earn you more points than scoring a goal, which is something I always stressed to my players. Nailing down the importance of both ends of the pitch is the narrative, whatever kind of run of results you are on, because games are won and lost there.

Coventry have made a poor start but what has happened in their first four games does not have to become the story of their whole season.

With Stoke, we got a win in our first home game - against Aston Villa - but that was our only victory in our first seven league matches after getting promoted.

The thing I remember most from that time is that Hull had come up with us and, after seven games, they had won at Newcastle , Arsenal and Tottenham and were in the top five in the table, while we were third or fourth from bottom.

I went out for dinner with my chairman, Peter Coates, and he said how Hull had made a wonderful start. I replied by telling him I bet you now that we finish above Hull... and we did.

The reason I thought that was because of the mindset of the team, and the fans.

I was confident my players were not going to go weak at the knees, and the togetherness we needed was already there in the squad, while the support was just off the scales, which helped us enormously at home.

Every defeat was taken on the chin, and accepted, but the lads were always ready to go, again and again.

It was Steve Coppell who said to me how you have to deal with the fact you are going to lose a lot of games - or at least not win a lot of them - when you take a team up into the Premier League.

It is a very unusual situation, to go from being in the Championship and winning regularly week after week, to dealing with defeat after defeat.

Steve told me to get ready for going on runs where we would not win for five or six games on the bounce, but then if we could win two or three games in the same period after that, we would fly up the table.

But getting your head around that is hard, and it is the same for the players who were part of that promotion - especially if you were dominant like Coventry were last season.

They were expected to challenge at the top of the Championship, but in my opinion over-achieved by finishing clear at the top.

It was different for Hull, who achieved a promotion under Sergej Jakirovic that no-one outside that club believed was possible.

They have started the season on fire, just like the Tigers did in 2008 when Phil Brown was in charge, and now they have to try to sustain it.

They are third at the moment but if they are 17th come the end of May, which is where they finished under Brownie, then that will be a successful season.

I will be taking a closer look at Hull's progress in this column in the weeks to come, as well as the other promoted team, Ipswich.

Gary O'Neil has a really tough gig at Portman Road but it is one he will relish. I gave Gary his senior debut with Portsmouth in the Championship in 1999 and he's a smart lad who was always football mad.

Ipswich are a great club and I hope both are successful this season. Gary has experience of the Premier League with Bournemouth and Wolves, and he is going to need it.

New season, nine new managers - which appointments make sense?

Including O'Neil, there are nine new managers starting with clubs in the Premier League. It's a bigger number than usual and I wanted to quickly run through all of them.

Enzo Maresca at Manchester City seemed like common sense to me, even before they started the season with four league wins out of four, because he has worked with Pep and the club before.

City had a large turnover of players with their ins and outs over the summer, but I'd expect them to be in the mix for all the trophies again this season.

Another place where lots of changes have taken place is Stamford Bridge. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has experience of playing in England and will understand that no game in the Premier League is a shoe-in - as Saturday's draw with Hull showed us again.

Andoni Iraola did an amazing job at Bournemouth but he will need all of his managerial ability and acumen to succeed at Liverpool .

At Liverpool , teams will drop deep and rely on counter-attacking situations. At Bournemouth that did not happen very often.

So, Andoni has to prepare his coaching philosophy to overcome teams who will definitely play deeper and be much more defensive-minded against Liverpool than they were against Bournemouth .

In my opinion, given time he will a great success but as he prepares to take his new team back to face his old one at Vitality Stadium on Sunday, we are already seeing that Liverpool will need more changes to develop into the title-winning side that their fantastic supporters demand.

At Nottingham Forest , Oliver Glasner did a wonderful job at Palace and I am sure we will see more of the same at the City Ground.

At the moment I know less about Marco Rose, Matthias Jaissle, and Pierre Sage, at Bournemouth , Newcastle and Crystal Palace .

Unlike the other managers I have mentioned, they have no experience of the Premier League but they are all joining established top-flight sides which is a huge help.

Finally, there is Alvaro Arbeloa at Fulham . He had a fantastic playing record at Real Madrid and Liverpool and coached in the Real Madrid academy and their B team before taking charge of the first team for the second half of last season.

While he has not had much experience in the dugout, he has worked with many top managers and players.

Fulham will be a real test for him, as we've seen from the way they have started the season, so again they are a club I will be keeping a close eye on - but there are plenty of those!

I got stuck into lots of topics in this column last season, at all levels of the game and covering every aspect of management, but I'd love to know what you would like me to talk about over the next few weeks.

Please make any suggestions in the comments section below - and also feel free to ask me any questions too.

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

articles.title: Owen Ndlovu: Abducted South African journalist found dead with gunshot wounds
articles.summary: The body of veteran broadcaster Owen Ndlovu was found hours after armed men kidnapped him near Johannesburg.
articles.body:
Tributes are pouring in for a veteran South African sports broadcaster who was found dead on Wednesday hours after being abducted when his vehicle was hijacked in a township near Johannesburg.

Owen Ndlovu, a former presenter with the country's public broadcaster, the SABC, was seized on Tuesday while collecting his wife from a church in Katlehong, police said.

His body, which witnesses said had gunshot wounds, was discovered by residents the following morning.

Police have launched a manhunt for three suspects and are investigating the circumstances surrounding his killing, which has once again drawn attention to South Africa's high levels of violent crime.

South African president vows justice as more women's bodies found near Johannesburg

South Africa's deadly love affair with guns

Provincial police spokesperson Col Dimakatso Nevhuhulwi said Ndlovu had gone to pick up his wife from a religious service when the attackers struck.

"As she approached their vehicle, three unknown men, one reportedly armed with a firearm, suddenly approached them, pushed her aside and forced her husband into the back seat," she said.

"The suspects then drove off with the victim."

The vehicle, a Ford Raptor pick-up truck - commonly known as a bakkie in South Africa - was later recovered abandoned in Walkerville, an area south of Johannesburg, police said.

Ndlovu's body was found by local residents beside a road in Thokoza, which neighbours Katlehong. They said he appeared to have suffered gunshot wounds.

A bag of his was found a few metres away.

Police said they were investigating a case of murder but a post-mortem examination would establish the cause of death.

"At this stage, the family is awaiting further information from the relevant authorities regarding the circumstances surrounding Owen's death," said family spokesperson Eugene Mthethwa.

The family described the loss as "devastating" and thanked residents, police and members of the public who had helped search for him after news of his abduction emerged.

Ndlovu was a familiar figure to South African sports fans after years working as a presenter and producer at the SABC.

He was also involved in radio coverage of the country's Premier Soccer League and later became an advocate for musicians' rights and royalty payments.

The 54-year-old was also associated with Artists United and the SABC Summer Song of the Year initiative.

Lelo Mzaca, a fellow journalist, remembered him as a man who lived a "colourful, energetic life" and brought enthusiasm and flair to sports broadcasting.

"South Africa has lost a unique and spirited individual whose light shone brightly while it lasted," Mzaca added in a tribute on the Mail & Guardian news site.

The provincial government urged communities to help police with the investigation, saying tackling crime remained a priority.

The killing has again drawn attention to violent crime in South Africa, where armed robberies and vehicle hijackings remain a major concern.

The latest national police figures, covering April to June 2026, recorded more than 5,000 murders and close to 4,000 carjackings.

When releasing the figures last month, acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia said serious crimes continued to create fear in communities and that some were carried out by "organised, heavily armed criminal groups that operate with planning and sophistication".

articles.summary: Florian Kohfeldt will return to Volkswagen Arena on the opening day of matchday 6 in 2. Bundesliga. The 43-year-old had an unsuccessful stint in Wolfsburg af...
articles.body:
Florian Kohfeldt will return to Volkswagen Arena on the opening day of matchday 6 in 2. Bundesliga. The 43-year-old had an unsuccessful stint in Wolfsburg after his coaching breakthrough with Werder Bremen .

Following their push for promotion last term, Kohfeldt's Darmstadt had a slow start this term. They had to wait until matchday 5 for a first league win of the season as Stoke City loanee Milan Smit scored a late winner against Arminia Bielefeld from the spot.

Meanwhile, Wolfsburg suffered their first defeat of the season a day later with Joel Fujita's winner for St. Pauli a couple of minutes before the end of regular time. Those two results closed the gap between these two sides to only four points.

The two clubs met only nine times before the upcoming fixture on Friday. Darmstadt's two wins came in front of their fans, while Wolfsburg were victorious in each of the last three encounters. Since this is the first 2. Bundesliga campaign for Wolfsburg in over three decades, it's a first head-to-head game in this division after 1993.

There are no new injury worries in both camps. Tobias Strobel's side will welcome Robert Glatzel back in the squad after the veteran striker missed last week's game in Hamburg . As for the visitors, summer signings Ho-Jae Lee and Smit will hope to keep their places up front after scoring against Bielefeld. Aleksander Vukotic will be back in Darmstadt's defense after a two-game suspension.

articles.title: When Moises Caicedo Could Make Chelsea Injury Return
articles.summary: Will Moises Caicedo make his Chelsea return in the upcoming trip to Brentford?
articles.body:
Moises Caicedo was absent for Chelsea 's draw against Hull City

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso will have to make a big decision on Moises Caicedo ahead of Friday's Premier League clash with Brentford .

Caicedo has been one of the four players on Chelsea's injury list in recent weeks, alongside summer signings Jordan Henderson , Marco Palestra , and Emmanuel Emegha .

The other three have yet to feature for Chelsea this season, while Caicedo missed the opening two matches and made his return against his former club, Brighton & Hove Albion , albeit very briefly.

Coming on as a substitute in the second half, the midfielder was forced off with an injury just 14 minutes later.

Alonso confirmed that Caicedo, who has not played since, is struggling with a calf issue.

Speaking before Saturday's 2-2 draw with Hull City , Alonso admitted he decided against taking the risk of playing Caicedo, who had yet to fully recover.

However, he also confirmed Caicedo might be ready for this upcoming derby.

"Let's see for Brentford, but unluckily not at the moment to take risks with him," Alonso said last week. "Not yet; we are not there yet."

Similarly, the other three could also be available to face Brentford, depending on their fitness.

The question is whether Alonso feels it is necessary to include any of these four. The away match against Brentford is going to be Chelsea's last fixture before the extended international break.

Letting these four recover for the next three weeks would arguably be the safest choice.

That said, Chelsea dropped points last weekend against Hull, and another disappointing result heading into the international break would dent the team's morale.

Caicedo's return, in particular, would certainly boost Chelsea's chances of beating Brentford amid the team's terrible defensive record.

Despite Reece James and Romeo Lavia 's commendable efforts in midfield, neither has Caicedo's ball-winning skills.

Aside from James and Lavia, Valentin Barco and Malo Gusto , who is naturally a right-back, are the other two midfield options. Barco has only played 29 Premier League minutes so far, and Gusto had a poor display against Hull.

Chelsea's lack of control in midfield, averaging just 44.2 per cent possession of the ball this season, arguably played a big part in the team's leaky defence, which has conceded nine goals in four league matches.

Brentford have been unbeaten since the start of the season, with two wins and three draws in all competitions. Sitting seventh in the league, one place behind Chelsea in sixth, Brentford are expected to be another tough challenge for Alonso's side.

articles.title: Press conference on Europa League opener: "It's what we've worked for!“
articles.summary: Danny Röhl and Dominik Schmid ahead of Levski SofiaOn the eve of our UEFA Europa League opener, we headed into the bowels of Sofia’s historic Vasil Levski Na...
articles.body:
Danny Röhl and Dominik Schmid ahead of Levski Sofia

On the eve of our UEFA Europa League opener , we headed into the bowels of Sofia's historic Vasil Levski National Stadium. There, head coach Danny Röhl and Dominik Schmid fielded questions from the media in a somewhat unusual setting - the official press conference was held, at short notice, in a former gym within the arena.

I'm definitely looking forward to the match. It's an interesting stadium with so much history. Levski have made a very good start to their league season, and were ultimately only eliminated in the final round of Champions League qualifying. They like to play football. It will be interesting because both teams share that philosophy. We're looking forward to it - the players have worked hard for this and are raring to go for the league phase

There are still two or three positions up for grabs. I'm weighing up a few different options and will make the final decision just before our final team meeting. Both teams will try to gain control of the game. Levski average over 60 percent possession in the league, much like us. It will come down to how effective our pressing is, how quickly we win the ball back, and how well we utilise our spells of possession to attack. It's not just about having possession, but also about how determined and purposeful we are going forward.

We've done our homework. We had people on the ground watching the opposition live. That's always different from watching on TV. We don't know exactly how many fans will turn up tomorrow, but there were reportedly 38,000 against Athens - and that creates a real cauldron-like atmosphere. The key is for our principles to take hold, for our patterns of play to click, and for us to play with high intensity and determination in our duels.

It's sure to be an exciting game. Right now, it's about getting into the best possible shape overnight and throughout the day tomorrow. Naturally, we want to kick off our Europa League campaign with a win.

On his role as a leader to the young players:

I don't really need to say anything special. If I feel it's necessary, I'll certainly speak up. But the young players have their own preparation routines and might want some peace and quiet to focus on the match. I've got a fair few European matches under my belt, but the young guys will do a great job too. If they need help, we older players and the coaching staff are definitely here for them.

Kick-off at the Vasil Levski National Stadium is on Thursday at 18:45 CEST (19:45 local time). For fans back home, the match will be broadcast live on Sky Sport Austria, on free-to-air TV via ServusTV, and via a live stream on ServusTV On. Fans around the world should check local broadcasters.

articles.body: El Real Betis y el Getafe se enfrentan este jueves 17 de septiembre desde las 19.00 horas en el Estadio de La Cartuja, en el partido correspondiente a la sexta jornada de LaLiga EA Sports. articles.title: Do Celtic have 'big issues', or will next four days hush concerns?
articles.summary: Chris Sutton believes his former side have "great concerns" despite a winning start to the Scottish Premiership season. The next four days will tell us wheth...
articles.body:
Football in Glasgow's goldfish bowl has a habit of being unnecessarily dramatised, yet there is a case for saying a week in mid-September could have a defining impact on Celtic's season.

After spectacularly failing the first of three tests during this mini crucial spell, alarm bells are ringing among sections of an unconvinced support.

Martin O'Neill's side have the chance to right the wrongs of their sobering 3-0 Premier Sports Cup quarter-final defeat by Rangers at Ibrox when they host their city rivals in a rematch in the league on Sunday, but a Europa League opener with Ferencvaros comes first.

Celtic fans are tiptoeing with trepidation into their first European action since their Champions League play-off collapse in Linz, a capitulation that has the same supporters questioning this team's big-game credentials, especially after Sunday.

"It's strange you're never asked about team selection when you win games," O'Neill responded bullishly when asked about the outside noise.

"We've been doing a fair amount of winning domestically now for quite some considerable time and we've won our league games so far.

"It's another big test for us on Sunday, obviously, but it's amazing the number of times you're not questioned when you've won."

In short: the aforementioned big-game results this season and the performance level under O'Neill since January.

The 74-year-old's remit last term was to end a chaotic, rollercoaster campaign on a high after the Wilfried Nancy debacle. He absolutely did that, winning the Scottish Premiership title and Scottish Cup.

Celtic fans spent the aftermath of that double triumph torn over whether they wanted to watch their legendary manager head off into the sunset with two medals round his neck or have him lead the team into a fresh season. Even O'Neill was unsure .

One thing supporters were united on, though, was wanting to see overdue progress in Europe and a better product on the pitch. It seems they are still waiting for that.

There will be fans of rival clubs who will view those wishes as greed, given Celtic still continue to dominate domestically.

However, supporters of the Parkhead side have spent the past decade being conditioned into watching their team clean up trophies while still delivering dominant, free-flowing football, hence the demand is there.

O'Neill and his staff were largely given a pass last term during a season of intense turbulence. Fury was mostly directed towards the club's hierarchy, but the manager and his backroom team are now not immune from scrutiny.

The Celtic boss's team selection has been questioned by fans and pundits, including one of his former players, Chris Sutton, in the wake of an abject derby display.

Are Sutton's 'great concerns' justified?

Below-par showings were forgiven last season as Celtic simply just had to get by to stay in touch at the top before eventually leapfrogging Heart of Midlothian on the final day with a seventh successive league victory.

That Premiership-winning streak has been extended to 13 games following six straight victories to start the campaign, but concerns about performance level remain. Four of those six wins have been by a one-goal margin.

Twelve goals over three wins at Kilmarnock, Dundee United and in the first leg of the Champions League play-off against LASK sent an ominous warning to Celtic's domestic rivals amid a period of high spending, particularly in forward areas.

Camilo Duran has been the standout summer recruit so far with six goals and three assists in 10 appearances, while record signing Kasper Hogh and fellow big-money arrival Haissem Hassan are yet to fully settle.

Sutton said his old club have been "flat-track bullies" by "beating the teams you expect them to beat", but the collapse in Austria , plus Sunday's bruising loss, has highlighted glaring deficiencies.

Even captain Callum McGregor lamented Celtic's "team of individuals" after the weekend defeat at Ibrox.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club , former striker Sutton also expressed his "great concerns" for O'Neill's men and said they have "big issues" after a "lightweight" midfield was "run all over" by Rangers.

Celtic have struggled to build up play against coherent pressing teams, which results in opposition sides being offered too much encouragement when the ball turns over.

They faced a whopping 60 shots across both legs with LASK. Forty of them came in a mess of a second leg. In the Premiership alone this season, they have faced 64 attempts, the same number as Hearts and six more than Rangers.

Over just six games, that tally already makes up almost a quarter of the total they faced in the entirety of the 2024-25 league-winning campaign under Brendan Rodgers.

That said, in comparison to last term, which was overseen by Rodgers, Nancy and O'Neill, Celtic's Premiership numbers show they are currently averaging a far better goal concession rate while scoring and shooting more.

Come Sunday, though, the most crucial statistic could be in the points column.

With a rapid rematch against Rangers offering the chance to move eight points clear of their city rivals after a test against European-level opposition, the next four days will at least be mood-shifting.

Whether that is to O'Neill's benefit remains unclear.

articles.title: Bayern's Hoeness: Kane must win Ballon d'Or
articles.summary: Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness believes Harry Kane should be the clear choice for this year's Ballon d'Or. "He would absolutely deserve it.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness believes Harry Kane should be the clear choice for this year's Ballon d'Or.

"He would absolutely deserve it. And I hope he gets it," Hoeness told the Abendzeitung newspaper.

The ceremony takes place on October 26 in London, with Kane up against the likes of Lamine Yamal , Rodri , Lionel Messi , Ousmane Dembélé and Kylian Mbappé .

Hoeness dismissed the idea of Messi winning the award again as "nonsense," arguing that Kane had enjoyed "an outstanding season across all competitions."

"If he doesn't deserve it this year, then when?" he said.

Hoeness also pointed to Mbappé, who finished as top scorer in both the Champions League and the World Cup but failed to win a title with Real Madrid .

"They didn't even become Spanish champions," the 74-year-old said. "They didn't win a single title - and we won two."

Kane, 33, won the Bundesliga and German Cup with Bayern, reached the Champions League semi-finals and captained England to third place at the World Cup.

He also won the European Golden Shoe as the continent's leading goalscorer and finished as the Bundesliga's top scorer for a third successive season with 36 goals.

Kane scored 73 competitive goals for club and country over the season.

Only Messi has scored more, with 82 goals for Barcelona and Argentina in the 2011-12 season.

There are no other candidates this year who clearly stand out through success in both the Champions League and the World Cup.

The last Bayern player to win the Ballon d'Or was Karl-Heinz Rummenigge 45 years ago in 1981, after also winning the award in 1980.

Franz Beckenbauer won it as a Bayern player in 1972 and 1976, while Gerd Müller took the award in 1970.
