articles.title: 'We can't just throw everything at Carrick' - Morrison
articles.summary: "We have to be careful to not go too over the top with this result," said former Premier League midfielder Jobi McAnuff after Manchester United threw away a...
articles.body:
"We have to be careful to not go too over the top with this result," said former Premier League midfielder Jobi McAnuff after Manchester United threw away a two-goal lead against Brighton in the Carabao Cup third round.

A section of United fans made their feelings clear with boos at full-time, with Michael Carrick's team having taken just two wins from six games in all competitions this season.

"Michael Carrick is incredibly experienced," McAnuff told BBC Radio 5 Live's Football Daily. "He will know the results haven't been anywhere near good enough this season and he will be concerned.

"You cannot win football games if you are conceding two or more goals every week - that is a big problem.

"Everybody at Brighton was on the same page but Manchester United were the complete opposite of that tonight. There were times when Leny Yoro or Ayden Heaven were on the ball but had no options. There was a real lack of cohesion and togetherness."

Former Premier League striker Clinton Morrison added: "The fans were not happy. It was a disappointing performance which they could have lost by more goals, to be fair.

"We can't just throw everything at Michael Carrick. We have to remember the job he did last season when Ruben Amorim was struggling.

"He obviously made changes to give some of his squad players a chance, but it just goes to show that his squad players are not good enough at the moment to have an influence.

"They are conceding goals in the Premier League as well. I don't think the issue is tactical. At the end of the day, they just haven't got it right at the moment."

articles.title: Barcelona president Joan Laporta wants 2030 World Cup final at Spotify Camp Nou: ‘I say this for one reason’
articles.summary: Barcelona president Joan Laporta has set his sights on another major international event for the refurbished Spotify Camp Nou after UEFA confirmed the stadiu...
articles.body:
Barcelona president Joan Laporta has set his sights on another major international event for the refurbished Spotify Camp Nou after UEFA confirmed the stadium as the venue for the 2029 Champions League final .

Laporta now wants FIFA to select Barcelona's home for the 2030 World Cup final, by which point the redevelopment is expected to be complete, and the stadium will have a capacity of around 105,000 spectators.

Speaking to SER Catalunya , the Barça president made his preference clear while addressing the possibility of the final being staged in Casablanca or Madrid.

"It shouldn't be Casablanca or Madrid; it should be the Spotify Camp Nou. Casablanca and Madrid are one and the same," he stated.

The Barcelona president believes the size of the completed stadium should be an important consideration for FIFA.

Laporta wants the 2030 World Cup final to be played at the Spotify Camp Nou. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

He also pointed to the fact that the 1982 World Cup final was already played at the Santiago Bernabéu.

"I say this for one reason: 105,000 spectators. I believe FIFA will take this into account. And besides… a World Cup final was already held at the Santiago Bernabeu in 1982."

Laporta also made clear that his argument is not intended to disregard Morocco, one of the co-hosts of the 2030 tournament.

"With all due respect to Morocco, the 2030 World Cup final should be played in Spain, and besides, Spain is a World Cup-winning team."

Barcelona want Camp Nou to become global stage

Camp Nou will host more than 100,000 fans after complete development. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images)

Laporta sees the proposed World Cup final as part of a bigger ambition to raise Barcelona's international profile.

"Hosting the 2030 World Cup final at the Spotify Camp Nou would be the kind of international recognition we want to achieve, and that is what we will propose.

"We will put forward these reasons and others that we are sure to come up with, " he emphasised.

His comments come after the stadium was selected to host the 2029 Champions League final, giving Barça another major fixture to look forward to once the redevelopment is complete.

articles.title: David Beckham explains why Lionel Messi deserves to win Ballon d’Or over Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe
articles.summary: After inspiring Inter Miami past Cruz Azul to land the Campeones Cup, Messi has been tipped to beat Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe for football’s...
articles.body:
Lionel Messi has been tipped by Sir David Beckham to win the Ballon d'Or for a ninth time after scoring his 100th Inter Miami goal to help defeat Cruz Azul and win the Campeones Cup.

Messi enjoyed a fine World Cup with Argentina reaching the final before defeat to champions Spain, with eight goals and four assists, alongside the milestone of becoming the all-time top scorer in the tournament's history before Kylian Mbappe eclipsed him after scoring in the bronze final.

And after the latest highlight in his American adventure, co-owner Beckham has lauded Messi's impact and tipped him to beat out the likes of Harry Kane , Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe for the top individual prize in the sport.

"I still can't believe we have him in Miami playing for our team," Beckham said. "That's why I go to training every day and watch him and turn up to watch him every time possible, we want to see Leo play football forever,"

"When you see him do things like tonight, and you see him have the World Cup he's had, it's not luck that he's being considered for the Ballon d'Or again. It's not luck. He was probably the best player in the tournament; he had an incredible year last year…

"At 39 years old, to affect the World Cup in every game the way he did, that's special. There's no one at 39 who is doing this at that level. He deserves to be considered for the Ballon d'Or. In my opinion, he should win it. You have great players in there, like Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham , and other players, but when talking about Leo, I'm his biggest supporter."

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, converting a Luis Suárez cross to bring up a century of goals in 115 appearances across all competitions.

Casemiro made it 2-0 in the 81st minute, heading in a corner from Messi.

The Brazilian midfielder has scored four goals, all headers, in his last five matches after scoring in three consecutive games against CF Montreal , Atlanta United and Chicago before being held scoreless Saturday against Nashville.

The victory gave Inter Miami another trophy three years after Messi's arrival. Miami won the Leagues Cup in 2023, the Supporters' Shield in 2024 and MLS Cup in 2025.

Inter Miami returns to MLS play Sunday when it hosts San Diego FC at Nu Stadium. Miami enters the match second in the Eastern Conference standings.

articles.title: Raúl Varela: "Mbappé ha perdido aura en sala de prensa"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu cuestiona las explicaciones del francés a la polémica de la camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu cuestiona las explicaciones del francés a la polémica de la camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta
articles.body: Raúl Varela analizó en La Tribu las explicaciones de Kylian Mbappé sobre lo ocurrido en los prolegómenos del partido en Elche. El periodista fue contundente con la intervención del delantero del Real Madrid y aseguró que el francés ya no transmite las mismas sensaciones cuando comparece ante los medios. "Ha perdido aura Kikí en sala de prensa, un escenario que dominaba casi como el área donde a pesar de sus incontables fallos sigue sumando goles cada jornada y es el claro candidato al Pichichi de la temporada", afirmó Varela. Varela se refirió a la explicación de Mbappé sobre lo sucedido antes del encuentro en Elche: "Kylian Mbappé nos intentaba convencer, sin éxito, de que lo ocurrido en los prolegómenos del partido en Elche fue un mix de sensibilidades y prioridades". Una explicación que, para el director de La Tribu, no sirvió para aclarar la polémica. "Si muchos no entendieron lo de la camiseta a media asta, después del churrivideo creo que se entiende todavía menos. Efecto contrario", señaló. Varela insistió en que el discurso del francés no terminó de resolver sus dudas: "Analizando su discurso no me ha quedado claro prácticamente nada". El periodista aprovechó para reiterar su postura sobre la participación de los futbolistas en este tipo de iniciativas. "Mantengo mi firme convencimiento de que los futbolistas no tienen ninguna obligación de adherirse a casi ninguna campaña. Ponerse la camiseta de su club y a jugar", explicó. "Lo otro tiene que ser algo tan extremadamente claro sobre lo que haya que postularse que todo lo demás es casi mejor evitarlo. No hablamos de un No al Racismo o a la guerra que eso no admite ni debate, ni discusión ni matiz", añadió. La crítica de Varela fue más allá al analizar la reacción posterior. "Lo que se demuestra es que viven ajenos al mundo, metidos en su burbuja, preocupados de sus cosas y siempre al margen del interés general", aseguró. También cuestionó la forma en la que se produjo la explicación: "Tantos millones y tantos asesores para tener que mal reaccionar a media tarde de forma casi clandestina con una explicación peregrina difícil de descifrar. ¿Ceuta? Of course. ¿Inmigrantes, pobreza o sufrimiento? Of course, también". Pese a sus críticas, Varela destacó la predisposición de Mbappé a hablar y posicionarse públicamente: "Siempre hay que agradecerle que no le tenga alergia al micrófono ni tampoco al posicionamiento en función de sus convicciones, por ejemplo en Francia y el auge de la ultraderecha". El director de La Tribu cerró su reflexión con una frase contundente sobre las explicaciones ofrecidas por el delantero madridista: "Pero lo de ayer es inexplicable, porque, obviamente no tiene explicación".

articles.title: Andy - the sniper
articles.summary: Some nights are so improbable that they become possible. Inter began their 2003 Champions League campaign away to Arsenal. In other words: an impossible miss...
articles.body:
Some nights are so improbable that they become possible. Inter began their 2003 Champions League campaign away to Arsenal . In other words: an impossible mission. Especially against that version of Arsene Wenger's Gunners, known as the Invincibles. They would finish the Premier League season unbeaten in all 38 matches, a record no one has matched since. It had happened only once before, with Preston North End in 1888-89, two centuries earlier.

Arsenal had Ljungberg and Pires, Bergkamp and Henry, Vieira and Kanu. Inter had undergone a revolution in the transfer market. "We need wingers," Hector Cuper had demanded. Four arrived: Kalilou Fadiga, who would never make his debut because of heart problems; Eriberto , who would soon return to Chievo; Kily Gonzales from Valencia ; and then a winger from Ajax who, just a few months earlier, had dazzled in the Champions League, among other things scoring a fantastic goal at the Olimpico. It was his celebration that had earned him the nickname the Dutch Sniper . Andy Van Der Meyde.

At Highbury, Arsenal's old, legendary stadium, he enjoyed his night of glory. Julio Cruz, who had arrived from Bologna to replace Hernan Crespo after his move to Ajax, opened the scoring. He looked like a replacement but proved to be a stroke of fortune: Julione would go on to win four Serie A titles, two Coppa Italia trophies and three Italian Super Cups with Inter. Arsenal started strongly, very strongly, but Toldo was having one of those nights that occasionally came his way in Europe in those years, like in Valencia a few months earlier. He saved everything. It was Inter who took the lead, through Cruz. Martins played a through ball, Cruz took it in his stride and produced a delightful touch to lift it over Seaman as the goalkeeper came off his line. Before the Londoners had even had time to work out what had happened, Inter scored again: Kily Gonzales crossed from the left, the defence headed it away and the ball looped up before slowly dropping. It looked as though it was about to hit the ground when a ferocious first-time right-foot strike sent it flying. Andy Van Der Meyde was the first to realise what had happened and raised his imaginary rifle. 0-2. There was still time for Francesco Toldo to cover himself in glory by saving a penalty from Thierry Henry . And there was still time to see Oba Martins steal the ball from Kolo Tourè and score one of those goals that are difficult to understand even in slow motion, with a unique but undoubtedly effective piece of coordination. Arsenal attacked in the second half, but the game was already over. In fact, Inter even came close to making it 0-4 late on.

"The Lions of Highbury," some newspapers called them the following day, a nickname that had originated in 1934, when the Italian national team had gone down fighting, losing 3-2 to England in a friendly; they had been reduced to ten men almost immediately, as substitutions did not exist. The two Italian goals? Both scored by Giuseppe Meazza.

Today, after a career that failed to live up to expectations, Andy Van Der Meyde has become a hugely influential figure on Instagram and is involved in various ventures. He often talks about his career, and has never had any doubts about its brightest moment. That night at Highbury when, for one night in Nerazzurri colours, he was the Dutch Sniper.

articles.title: Beckham backs Messi for Ballon d'Or after 100th Miami goal
articles.summary: Lionel Messi deserves to win a ninth Ballon d'Or after guiding Argentina to the World Cup final and scoring his 100th Inter Miami goal, says former England c...
articles.body:
Lionel Messi deserves to win this year's Ballon d'Or, according to Inter Miami co-owner and former England captain David Beckham.

The 39-year-old Argentina great, who has won the global player of the year award eight times and has been nominated on the 30-player shortlist for 2026, scored his 100th goal for Miami on Wednesday.

He also provided an assist for Casemiro to score their second goal in a 2-0 victory over Cruz Azul that clinched the Campeones Cup - an annual match contested by US and Mexican cup winners.

"When you see him do things like this, when you see him have the World Cup that he's had, there is no one at 39 that's doing that, and doing it at that level," said Beckham.

"He deserves to be considered for the Ballon d'Or. In my opinion, he should win it."

Messi scored eight goals and registered four assists as he helped Argentina reach the 2026 World Cup final, where they were beaten by Spain.

He took his career assists tally to 12 in World Cups, of which 10 have come in the knockout rounds. No other player on record has more than eight in total.

He is the second-highest goalscorer in World Cup history, with 21, behind the 22 scored by France's Kylian Mbappe .

Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane is one of three England players nominated for the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

Real Madrid 's Jude Bellingham and Arsenal 's Declan Rice join Kane, the favourite for the award, on the 30-player shortlist.

Lamine Yamal is one of six Spain players that won the World Cup to be included.

Having scored the winning goal in the final, Paris St-Germain forward Ferran Torres , who joined the French club from Barcelona in the summer, makes the cut.

Back-to-back Champions League winners PSG have nine players - excluding new signing Torres - nominated, including last year's winner Ousmane Dembele .

Real Madrid forwards Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr also make the shortlist, as do Arsenal defenders Gabriel and William Saliba .

The award is celebrating its 70th anniversary, having been created by France Football in 1956, and the winner will be announced at a ceremony in London on 26 October.

Messi opened the scoring in Wednesday's Campeones Cup match at their Nu Stadium when he headed in a Luis Suarez cross in the 24th minute.

He thought he had added a second when he raced clear on goal and slotted in a shot, only for the effort to be disallowed for offside.

However, Messi great delivered the corner from which former Real Madrid and Manchester United midfielder Casemiro headed in their second goal in the 81st minute to give Miami their first Campeones Cup.

His exploits came after August's announcement that he was retiring from international football, and after saying he was considering his future in football following the death of his father, Jorge.

"We have to enjoy this because we don't know how long we'll have it," said Casemiro.

"What he has done and continues to do for football is incredible. He remains the best. He proved it at the World Cup and continues to prove it in MLS."

articles.title: Roberto Gómez: "Camello tiene que ir a la selección"
articles.standfirst: El colaborador de La Tribu apuesta por el delantero de cara a la próxima lista, reclama el regreso de Fermín y se rinde al momento del Barça: "Es un auténtico espectáculo"
articles.summary: El colaborador de La Tribu apuesta por el delantero de cara a la próxima lista, reclama el regreso de Fermín y se rinde al momento del Barça: "Es un auténtico espectáculo"
articles.body: La próxima lista de la selección española fue uno de los grandes asuntos de la conversación entre Raúl Varela y Roberto Gómez en La Tribu. Con la convocatoria en el horizonte, Roberto puso varios nombres encima de la mesa y fue especialmente contundente con uno de ellos: Sergio Camello. "Yo llevaría a Sergio Camello, por ejemplo, que creo que se lo merece. Por eso lo llevo reivindicando", aseguró Roberto Gómez. La retirada de Marcos Llorente también obliga, en su opinión, a buscar alternativas: "Hay que buscar un lateral o mediocampista o un hombre polifacético por Llorente". Otro de los jugadores por los que apostó fue Fermín. "Fermín tiene que estar en la selección", afirmó, antes de insistir en que "debe volver". Roberto también puso sobre la mesa otra posibilidad: "Me gustaría que fuera Espí, el jugador del Real Madrid. También se lo merece. Pero un poquito más Camello, creo yo". Su apuesta por Camello viene de lejos. "Lo llevo diciendo desde el primer día, que Camello tiene que ir a la selección", recordó. Además, destacó su relación previa con los técnicos de la Federación y su trayectoria con España: "Es un futbolista muy del gusto del seleccionador y sobre todo de Santi Denia". El colaborador de La Tribu considera que ha llegado el momento de empezar a mirar también hacia adelante. "De cara al futuro se tiene que ir ya pensando", señaló antes de destacar la importancia del próximo encuentro frente a Inglaterra en Londres: "Es un partidazo, es un partidazo, partidazo". Roberto también habló de la portería de la Selección ante las molestias de Joan García y puso dos alternativas encima de la mesa: "Podría llamar a Remiro, que forma parte de su grupo, y si no, a Leo Román". Sobre este último aseguró que "me parece el portero español más prometedor dentro de los jóvenes".

articles.body:
Real Madrid are among the clubs trying to sign Manchester United academy player JJ Gabriel.

Earlier this week, the 15-year-old sent United formal notice he wants to cancel his registration with immediate effect, but the club can challenge the request.

It is understood a number of major teams across Europe, including Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Bayern Munich, have a firm interest in the forward, but multiple sources have described Real's efforts to sign him as strong.

The Spanish side want to recruit the teenager immediately and position him in Real Madrid Castilla - the club's recognised reserve team.

Unlike in England, Castilla play in senior football and are in the regionalised third league of the Spanish system. Last season, they were coached by Alvaro Arbeloa, who then took over the senior Real side following Xabi Alonso's dismissal and has since moved to Fulham .

Thiago Pitarch, who was 18 at the start of last season, played for Castilla in a Premier League International Cup encounter against Southampton in October, and made 16 senior appearances across the campaign.

Sources close to Gabriel, who turns 16 on 6 October, feel let down by United, arguing promises around the pathway to the first team have not been kept.

The club say it was anticipated Gabriel would become their youngest senior player by playing in Wednesday night's EFL Cup tie with Brighton . Given they lost 3-2 after leading 2-0, it is debatable whether that would have actually happened.

United have not given up hope of keeping Gabriel, though they are unsure precisely why he wants to leave.

It is understood the player is not currently training with the club.

What next for Gabriel and Man Utd? Published 21 hours ago

What are the Premier League rules for academy players?

Speaking after the Brighton game, head coach Michael Carrick, who gave the youngster his senior debut during the pre-season match with Atletico Madrid in Stockholm said everyone needed to be mindful of Gabriel's age.

"I just think we've got to be really careful of the whole situation," he said.

"He's a young boy. He's 15, and for me, definitely, and from a club point of view, looking after our younger players - their welfare, their well-being, their exposure - we've got to be really conscious of that in this situation."

Sources close to Gabriel have dismissed concerns over the player's age and physicality and feel the likes of Max Dowman, who made his debut for Arsenal at the age of 15 last season, show a willingness to trust youth in a way they do not see at United.

Chelsea are also believed to have a major interest in the teenager.

Any imminent move away from Old Trafford for Gabriel is complicated because of rules regarding the registration of young players.

United say Gabriel's registration runs to the end of the season. It would be easier for him to leave United then, when he will be 16.

However, as Gabriel has an EU passport, it is possible he will be allowed to join a club within European Union borders on his 16th birthday.

articles.title: Has Romeo Lavia finally arrived at Chelsea after injury setbacks?
articles.summary: Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia says he is finally reaping the rewards of his hard work and is determined to "change the narrative" around him.
articles.body:
Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia says he is finally reaping the rewards of his hard work, feeling "free" again and determined to "change the narrative" around him.

Now 22, the Belgian is on the verge of enjoying his longest spell in the Chelsea side and, if he completes 60 minutes against Brentford on Friday, will surpass his previous best run of 518 minutes without injury - including pre-season matches.

Such progress has been some time in the making. Lavia made only one appearance in his first season at Chelsea because of a serious hamstring injury.

In his second campaign, he suffered a series of setbacks and missed 33 games, down from 42 the previous season, before significantly improving his availability last term by featuring in about half of Chelsea 's matches.

He has now remained available throughout pre-season and the opening weeks of the new campaign.

"There is so much that goes on behind the scenes," Lavia told BBC Sport - adding that he has a checklist he likes to tick off to ensure he is in the best condition for any given match.

"It's a big process but we're doing well at the moment."

It has been about overcoming the mental toll of repeated setbacks, but also avoiding becoming risk-averse - with manager Xabi Alonso encouraging Lavia to overcome the "mental block" of completing 90 minutes during a pre-season match against AC Milan in August.

"I've learned you can always go further than you think you can. You can always push your limits, especially when you feel like everything is going against you," he said.

"It's always easy to think about giving up, or to feel that whatever you do will take you back to the same point where you started.

"But luckily, with the help of team-mates, staff, everyone at the club and people close to me outside football, we've been able to create a sort of bubble where you concentrate only on what you can control."

With Reece James and Wesley Fofana having come through similar injury setbacks, Lavia is keen to become the latest Chelsea player to rewrite his story.

He has become a regular in Alonso's midfield alongside captain James, who began his career as a right-back.

Lavia's importance has only increased, with Moises Caicedo limited to 14 minutes this season and Enzo Fernandez having left for Manchester City in a £125m transfer on deadline day.

He added: "It's part of my game as well to take responsibility and have some character. I really like being in that position and also being at this club. Having this responsibility, it's not even pressure, it's just like privilege, so I'm actually living the dream.

"This is why you've been playing and training all these years for, so just go and enjoy it."

He speaks of having the "love" of his team-mates, while Chelsea have publicly and privately backed Lavia to become a key player despite an injury-hit couple of seasons.

There is now hope that Chelsea can become a force again after a tweaked transfer strategy that has added more experienced players, alongside the arrival of £117m club record signing Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa , who featured with Lavia in Manchester City 's academy.

Alongside Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro, Chelsea have scored 18 goals in all competitions across six matches, something that has thrilled Blues fans and neutrals alike.

"It's honestly amazing," Lavia said. "Obviously I knew Morgan, but just the way he's come in and then they've all clicked together up front. Sometimes I wish I could go in the stands and enjoy watching it.

"It makes your job easier, because it's like 'you guys go and work your magic and then we do the rest'. So we're really, really happy to have them all and hopefully we can achieve great things together."

Yet Lavia is not getting carried away and says the team have been "too immature" in the past and need to be "realistic" about "becoming the team that we and everyone thinks we can be".

For him, it is about ticking off milestones and enjoying the journey, both collectively and individually, after scoring his first Chelsea goal in a 4-3 win against Brighton .

"It was just a moment where I felt free," he explained. "It feels like all the work that you're putting in, you gain the reward of it, so it was a very emotional moment.

"I wanted to change the narrative. My first Premier League goal was against Chelsea [for Southampton in 2022], so I always felt like it was a bit strange.

"I saw all my team-mates score, so I was waiting for it to be my turn and when it happened I was very, very happy and excited. I wanted to express it as much as possible with the fans and I really loved it."

articles.title: "Tiene más merito lo que está haciendo Mourinho que el Barcelona"
articles.standfirst: Raúl Varela no ve al equipo de Flick tan superior al Real Madrid como se está diciendo después del arranque de temporada
articles.summary: Raúl Varela no ve al equipo de Flick tan superior al Real Madrid como se está diciendo después del arranque de temporada
articles.body: Ricardo Reyes, Ferran Martínez, Ricardo Rosety, Pablo Pinto, Nacho Labarga y Yon Cuezva han sido los tertulianos de este jueves en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada y con Raúl Varela a la cabeza, para analizar lo que ha dado de sí la jornada de LaLiga con el poderío del Barcelona y el triunfo del Atlético de Madrid. Raúl Varela. "Tiene más merito lo que está haciendo Mourinho que el Barcelona. Con nuevo entrenador y con media plantilla buena. Lo que hace el Madrid es muy meritorio y debería hacerlo incluso mejor. El Barça solo ha tenido más puntería que el Real Madrid". Ricardo Reyes. "Poner un pero después de un 7-2 es una cosa fea. Me hubiera gustado ver al Racing con todo, pero no hubiera cambiado mucho". Ferran Martínez. "El Barça hace cambios y no se nota. Los que salen mantienen el nivel y eso es mérito de Flick, que por primera vez tiene fondo de armario. Menos el portero, todos están a un nivel impresionante". Ricardo Rosety. "Si hace dos meses os dicen lo de Raphinha, ¿quién no se sorprende?". Pablo Pinto. "En lo que sí se parece este Barça al de Guardiola es que se va a ir a lo de los 100 puntos. Con los dedos de una mano salen los partidos en los que el Barça puede pinchar". Nacho Labarga. "No lo veo muy diferente al año pasado, pero la delantera está enchufadísima. Que el Racing juegue con nueve suplentes es para analizarlo. Ni el Barça es tan bueno, ni en el Madrid son tan malos. La distancia no es real". Yon Cuezva. articles.title: Adeyemi seduce al Spotify Camp Nou con números espectaculares
articles.standfirst: El alemán dio una asistencia, provocó dos penaltis y fue un dolor de cabeza para la zaga rival
articles.summary: El alemán dio una asistencia, provocó dos penaltis y fue un dolor de cabeza para la zaga rival
articles.body: Adeyemi se divirtió ayer en el Spotify Camp Nou y la afición disfrutó con el rápido atacante alemán. Es cierto que no pudo redondear su gran actuación con un tanto, pero dejó numerosos detalles de calidad y unos números que reflejan el gran protagonismo que tuvo durante los 90 minutos. Firmó ocho remates, completó 36 pases, realizó seis regates, provocó dos penaltis y dio una asistencia. A todo ello hay que añadir su principal arma: una velocidad endiablada. El alemán fue uno de los grandes protagonistas de una noche en la que el Barcelona encontró en su banda una fuente constante de peligro. Cada vez que recibió el balón con metros por delante, Adeyemi daba sensación de mucho peligro. "Da mucho y tiene mucho margen para adaptarse a nuestra filosofía. Nos da mucho, como hemos visto contra el Racing. Ha tenido a todos los culés detrás. No pasaba un buen momento en Alemania. Y además es un chico que cae bien en el vestuario. Tiene gran velocidad", destacó Hansi Flick después del encuentro. Desde el minuto uno, la banda de Adeyemi fue un auténtico dolor de cabeza para el Racing. El atacante se mostró eléctrico, buscando constantemente la espalda y generando espacios. Además, se entendió muy bien con Cancelo. Precisamente, poco antes del primer gol del luso, de hecho, volvió a exhibir su potencia en una carrera en la que se marchó por velocidad y terminó poniendo un buen balón para Raphinha, aunque no marcó el brasileño. El alemán estuvo cerca de encontrar el premio del gol en el minuto 19. Adeyemi intentó sorprender al guardameta con una picadita que terminó saliendo fuera por muy poco. No dejó de insistir y, al filo del descanso, volvió a ser protagonista al provocar un penalti que finalmente no pudo transformar Lamine Yamal. Tras el paso por los vestuarios, y pese a la intensa lluvia que cayó sobre el Spotify Camp Nou, Adeyemi mantuvo el mismo nivel de intensidad. Lejos de acusar el desgaste de una primera parte muy exigente, continuó atacando los espacios. Su insistencia tuvo de nuevo recompensa cuando provocó otra pena máxima, esta vez convertida por Raphinha. A esas alturas, el alemán se había convertido en una auténtica pesadilla para la zaga visitante y la afición aplaudía cada acción del azulgrana. Cada arrancada generaba expectación en las gradas. Y todavía tuvo fuerzas para aparecer en los últimos minutos, dando un gol a Lamine Yamal. Además, Adeyemi volvió a dejar una de esas acciones acrobáticas que ya comienzan a convertirse en una de sus señas de identidad. El alemán, que ya había intentado rematar de tacón durante el encuentro disputado en el Ciutat de València, volvió a probar suerte con un remate espectacular que tampoco terminó en gol. El balón no encontró portería, pero la acción recibió el aplauso de una grada que disfrutó con cada una de las ocurrencias del atacante. El alemán ha tenido minutos en todos los encuentros de esta temporada y ha sido titular en tres de ellos: Elche, Feyenoord y Racing de Santander. Además, suma tres dianas. Un buen arranque de curso para uno de los fichajes culés de la 26-27.

articles.title: Courtois se mete de lleno en el pádel
articles.standfirst: Nxtplay, la plataforma de negocio fundada por el portero belga y su socio Gonzalo Vila invertirá en el mundo del pádel con un proyecto que dará a conocer antes de que acabe el año
articles.summary: Nxtplay, la plataforma de negocio fundada por el portero belga y su socio Gonzalo Vila invertirá en el mundo del pádel con un proyecto que dará a conocer antes de que acabe el año
articles.body: Nxtplay, la compañía creada por el guardameta del Real Madrid Thibaut Courtois junto a su socio Gonzalo Vila, prepara su desembarco en el sector del pádel. La empresa prevé presentar un nuevo proyecto relacionado con este deporte antes de que termine el año y mantiene además la mirada puesta en dos de las grandes ligas estadounidenses: la NBA y la NFL. Courtois y Vila estuvieron presentes esta semana en la segunda y última jornada del un foro de fútbol. Durante su participación en este encuentro, centrado en la industria deportiva, ambos repasaron algunas de las líneas de crecimiento que maneja Nxtplay de cara a los próximos años. Uno de los anuncios llegó de la mano de Vila, que confirmó la apuesta de la compañía por el pádel, un deporte que atraviesa una etapa de fuerte expansión internacional. "Está creciendo mucho y está totalmente relacionado con cosas que estamos haciendo en lo comercial y de negocio", señaló el cofundador de Nxtplay, una plataforma que ya cuenta con intereses en otros ámbitos como el automovilismo y la propiedad de clubes de fútbol. Aunque Vila no quiso entrar en demasiados detalles, sí explicó que la iniciativa estará vinculada a la gestión deportiva y a la representación del talento dentro del mundo del pádel. "Es algo seguro que antes de que acabe el año añadiremos a nuestro porfolio", aseguró. La estrategia de Nxtplay también contempla reforzar su presencia en los eSports, un sector que encaja con la vertiente tecnológica y digital que busca potenciar la compañía. Con esta nueva operación, Courtois se suma a la creciente lista de futbolistas que han apostado por el pádel como vía de inversión, entre ellos Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo y Robert Lewandowski.

articles.title: Manchester United: What's to blame for latest problems and  results increasing scrutiny on Michael Carrick after Carabao Cup exit?
articles.summary: Michael Carrick is under increasing scrutiny at Manchester United; Man Utd have crashed out of the Carabao Cup and have produced their joint-worst start to a Premier League season; Vote on what you think the main issue is at Old Trafford below
articles.body:
United led 2-0 after just 10 minutes against Brighton on Wednesday night. By full-time, they had lost 3-2, exited the Carabao Cup at the third-round stage for a second successive season and been booed off by their own supporters.

It was the first time in 50 years United had lost at Old Trafford after going 2-0 up. They had won 143 of the previous 145 matches in which they had established that advantage. They also failed to register another shot on target after Mason Mount's 2-0 goal until the 76th minute.

The defeat leaves Carrick under pressure only months after his interim spell was rewarded with the permanent job. He had won 12 of his 17 matches last season, drawing three and losing two, giving him a 70.6 per cent win rate. This season, his record is two wins, one draw and three defeats from six games - a 33.3 per cent win rate.

United have now also matched their joint-worst start to a Premier League season after four games, while their Carabao Cup exit has removed an opportunity for silverware.

So what is the main issue at Old Trafford?

United's lack of urgency on the pitch has been stark, and the numbers match what we're seeing in matches.

United rank 14th in the Premier League for distance covered this season, with 449.1km, but their rankings drop sharply when the intensity of those movements is measured.

They are 18th for sprints, with 379, 19th for high-speed runs, with 1,364, 18th for sprints per kilometre covered and 19th for high-speed runs per kilometre.

That paints a picture of a team covering ground without doing enough of it at the speeds required to press, recover and defend transitions.

It was particularly obvious against Brighton. United's nine changes from the side that started the Manchester derby provided some context, with several players coming into the team after spending time on the bench. But Brighton also made six changes, including four players making their first starts for the club.

Jamie Redknapp questioned United's physical condition.

"They didn't look fit enough," he said. "I don't know if a lot of them do enough. I saw too many players not running back or not looking fit enough."

Leny Yoro's recovery for Brighton's third goal was one example. He was jogging back as Brighton broke, rather than sprinting into a position from which he could make a challenge.

It is a concern that stretches beyond one night. If United cannot match opponents for intensity, they are left defending larger spaces and spending longer without the ball.

Bomer86: "Why are Brighton fitter and faster than Man Utd? What is happening in training that the players are not fit? They were slower to every ball. No desire, no energy after 10 mins."

Ossy: "Fitness/intensity and Carrick's inability to read game state and react accordingly is going to be Man Utd's undoing this season."

United have spent, but is the squad balanced?

This summer United made seven permanent signings, alongside four loan arrivals, while 13 players left permanently and 10 went out on loan.

The headline investment has been concentrated heavily in midfield and attack. Around £85m of that spending started against Brighton in Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, while Carlos Baleba - signed from Brighton for around £70m - was watching from the stands.

The broader squad remains one of the most valuable in the Premier League. Transfermarkt values United's first-team squad at £791.2m , the fifth-highest figure among the clubs shown, behind Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool.

However, concerns remain over whether the distribution of that value has provided Carrick with enough tools to work with.

United's forwards account for £317.2m of the squad valuation and midfielders another £249.9m . The defensive group is valued at £193.8m , with the goalkeeper position accounting for the remainder.

The defence was already an obvious area of concern before the transfer window closed, yet United went into Wednesday's game with two inexperienced centre-backs in Yoro and Ayden Heaven and limited options at full-back.

EmmaRachael: "Why do Man Utd persist in buying quantity instead of real quality."

Cheese: "Appalling defence please invest in defensive reinforcements."

Gazza D: "United haven't backed Carrick. Desperately need two wing-backs of quality and that is evident in what we've seen with Dalot and Mazraoui."

Supporters have repeatedly questioned the direction of the club, particularly after another transfer window in which significant money was spent but defensive reinforcements remained an issue.

United have now cycled through several managers since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement, yet familiar complaints about the squad, recruitment and performances remain.

That is why Carrick's position can't be judged in isolation. The manager is responsible for the team on the pitch, but the squad he is selecting was built through decisions made at board and recruitment level.

S. Prime09: "United had a real chance to build on last season. The transfer window was so important. But we wouldn't spend over £70m. And all our top targets went some other team."

Ziggy: "The club has been lacking a clear plan since Fergie left. They don't know what they're doing."

Carrick: From interim hero to man under pressure

Carrick's interim spell last season was impressive enough to earn him the permanent job.

But it is the nature of the performances that has caused concern as much as the results.

United have struggled to control games and Carrick has faced questions over his in-game management and team selection. His nine changes against Brighton left him open to criticism when United's performance deteriorated after the early two-goal burst.

He accepted full responsibility for United's abject performance after the game.

"We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it," Carrick told Sky Sports. "The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me."

Jefft: "I'm so grateful for Carrick getting us into the top four but I said it then, the club should have said thanks but get in an elite coach who tactically has it."

Jon S: "At what point do you stop blaming managers and start blaming players? You can't keep swapping manager after manager after manager."

Wednesday's game exposed perhaps the clearest squad weakness. Yoro and Heaven formed an inexperienced centre-back pairing and Brighton repeatedly found space around them.

For the second goal, Luka Vuskovic won the header ahead of Benjamin Sesko, and the ball fell to Pascal Gross, who had space to finish. Heaven failed to anticipate the danger and Yoro could not prevent the shot.

For the third, Yoro was again caught behind the play as Brighton broke.

Full-back remains another concern, with Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui facing criticism for their positioning and distribution - and the depth behind the established defensive options remains questionable.

John S: "The gaps between Heaven and Yoro were too big, the full backs were beyond poor and the midfield looks average."

HN: "Why would you use an inexperienced back line in a must win game? Nothing against playing young players but pair them with experience."

Last season, United had a more settled attacking combination with Matheus Cunha on the left, Bryan Mbeumo through the middle and Amad Diallo on the right. Sesko remained an option introduced off the bench.

Rashford's return has altered that balance, with supporters questioning whether the change has affected the team's attacking rhythm.

The time without a shot on target against Brighton is a major concern: after the early burst, United could not consistently supply Sesko or create enough pressure to prevent Brighton from taking control.

Rashford did have a late chance to equalise but saw his near-post effort saved.

Dhanyaal: "Last season Cunha on left and Mbeumo on right and Sesko as number 9 was working. Why's he changed it and put Rashford on left?"

Platty7: "Rightly or wrongly the major change from last season is Rashford, he hasn't exactly set the world alight."

articles.title: Raphinha a Lamine: "Mi Balón de Oro"
articles.standfirst: El brasileño hace 'campaña' por el canterano culé
articles.summary: El brasileño hace 'campaña' por el canterano culé
articles.body: Raphinha nunca ha escondido el gran cariño y la excelente relación que mantiene con Lamine Yamal. El brasileño ha vuelto a demostrarlo este jueves en redes sociales, aprovechando una publicación del joven canterano para mostrarle públicamente su apoyo en la carrera por el Balón de Oro. El delantero azulgrana respondió a las imágenes que Lamine Yamal compartió del encuentro disputado el miércoles contra el Racing de Santander con un mensaje tan breve como contundente: "Eres un fenómeno. Mi Balón de Oro", escribió Raphinha. Unas palabras que reflejan la admiración que el internacional brasileño siente por su compañero y que, además, pueden interpretarse como un claro respaldo a su candidatura al prestigioso galardón individual. No es la primera vez que Raphinha se pronuncia en este sentido. La relación entre ambos jugadores va más allá del terreno de juego y se ha hecho especialmente visible durante los últimos meses. De hecho, los dos están siendo una dupla letal en este arranque de temporada. En el Barcelona, el respaldo hacia el futbolista es prácticamente unánime. Jugadores, técnicos y diferentes estamentos del club no han dudado en poner en valor sus actuaciones cuando han sido preguntados por sus opciones de conquistar el premio.

articles.title: El Granada sigue esperando al mejor Arnaiz
articles.standfirst: El atacante rojiblanco aún no ha mostrado su versión más determinante
articles.summary: El atacante rojiblanco aún no ha mostrado su versión más determinante
articles.body: Se está hablando mucho en este inicio de temporada de los jugadores más jóvenes y de cómo han irrumpido en el primer equipo con carácter y madurez. Pero para que todos los engranajes funcionen a la perfección, el Granada necesita la mejor versión de otras piezas como José Arnaiz, futbolistas experimentados que deben liderar al conjunto rojiblanco y aportar ese extra de competitividad. Arnaiz llegó el curso pasado a Los Cármenes para convertirse en la piedra angular del proyecto rojiblanco. Aunque le costó algo arrancar, el talaverano fue asumiendo galones hasta convertirse en el líder de los de Pacheta, asumiendo la responsabilidad ofensiva del equipo para acabar con 9 goles y 2 asistencias. Como le ocurrió en su primera campaña en el Granada, le está costando coger temperatura en estos primeros compases de la competición. Aún no ha sido capaz de desplegar todas sus virtudes, algo que ha echado en falta el equipo, sobre todo en encuentros que se han atascado y en los que la calidad del atacante podía haber marcado la diferencia. Con Bamba lesionado, Rodelas reubicado al extremo diestro y con Alemañ ocupando la mediapunta, Arnaiz se ha visto relegado a la zona izquierda del ataque, una posición escorada que limita su juego, le obliga a más esfuerzos para eliminar rivales y le permite prodigarse menos con su gran golpeo. La combinación disminuye su influencia en ataque y, por el momento, le ha impedido marcar o asistir. Por lo visto en estas primeras jornadas, Pacheta aún debe refinar un poco más su propuesta para que, más allá de la exigencia individual que debe asumir cada jugador, los mecanismos ofensivos sean más naturales y el potencial de cada futbolistas pueda aflorar con una mayor facilidad.

articles.title: Man City vs Liverpool: Why graduating from WSL winner to champion is so important to Alex Greenwood
articles.summary: In conversation with Sky Sports before the start of the season, Man City captain Alex Greenwood explains her desire to lead a team of champions - not just winners; watch Man City vs Liverpool live on Sky Sports+ on Friday; kick-off 7pm
articles.body:
Beginning the new campaign with back-to-back victories - the only team to do so - is testament to Greenwood's belief that there is a clear distinction between being a winner and being a champion. Becoming a champion is a process of progression, one that can only be achieved by consistently backing up what has already been accomplished.

Only one side has maximum points after the first two match rounds of this term, something that has not happened since 2015. Already, the WSL holders appear to be the ones to beat, picking up their baton and attacking the first leg of the race like consummate professionals. They have left the red half of Manchester for dust.

Greenwood herself has been a pillar of consistency under Andree Jeglertz. The beauty of this Manchester City team, actually, is how the sum of all its parts makes such a complete whole, bound together by one guiding rule: "We always find a way".

In conversation at Man City's training base, before a ball was kicked, the 32-year-old explains that her approach to this season will be framed differently. Because you are title holders, I surmise, rather presumptuously? Not the case.

"I needed a mental switch off," she replies, "this summer I had freedom, no schedule, and that is why I feel so fresh now. I can't remember the last time I got that long off, so I definitely enjoyed it."

Plenty changed for Greenwood over her summer of rest, not least getting engaged to long-term partner Jack, despite trying to bail on the plans they had on the evening of the proposal, not knowing what was about to happen.

"If I'm being really honest, the day of, I tried to cancel plans," she continues, smiling at the thought of it. "I wasn't in the mood to go out. But Jack told me he'd paid a heavy deposit on the restaurant. He played it very cool, didn't give much away, and it was amazing."

Beyond that, Greenwood describes this summer as a "necessary reset". The responsibility she carries as a captain means she constantly has "tabs open", unable to completely switch off from the demands of her own high standards as well as the team's. Like a never-ending homework assignment.

"I'm not the kind of person to turn it all off, I'm on the majority of the time. I reflect a lot. I needed a break, because a captain has a huge role off the pitch. But I'm lucky with the dressing room we have, it's an open environment to speak. I'm not the only one with the authority to make big calls."

Ruminating on last season should conjure fond memories. City were the dominant force, WSL leaders from early November and worthy winners of their first title in a decade. The football was freer, more inventive - guided by Jeglertz's philosophy rather than burdened by it.

Reinvention happened all over the pitch, from player to player, game to game. Opponents braced before playing City, not knowing what to expect or how to predict their ever-evolving patterns of play. Even when they were unremarkable, they almost always got the job done.

"I get asked a lot about pressure, and certain results made for pressure moments last season. We don't enjoy to lose. But in reality, we were in control. That helps with your preparation, with everything really. We had setbacks but we also had a safety net. That is what we do, always find a way."

City have edge now, a brand of nastiness that felt absent in previous title chases despite getting close. They did not need complete overhaul. "The manager made subtle differences with big results," Greenwood says. Jeglertz describes the adjustment as "never being satisfied", an unappeasable need to improve to a painstaking level of detail.

"He's very open to challenge," Greenwood adds. "He invites it. He wants us to challenge him and each other. It's such a competitive league. Teams have strengthened so much this summer, I love it. We remind each other we are winners, that fuels us to want to remain that. But we have huge respect for the level of opposition we face."

Man City have momentum on their side. They have developed multiple solutions for most problems. Gone are the days where their mental toughness is questioned after one stray result. The complication now is to maintain standards across every competition while also playing in Europe.

"I live for European nights," Greenwood says, touching on her frustration at having to watch last season's Champions League play out from her living room. "Do you know how hard it is to watch those games and not be involved?"

These are questions with implications that extend well beyond pre-season. How will City cope with the increased demands? Can they adapt to the relentless rhythm of three games a week? And does the squad possess enough depth and quality to compete on every front?

"We weren't there last year and we have to use that feeling to our advantage," insists Greenwood. "We cannot waste our opportunity."

City spent a decade trying to unlock the secret to becoming a WSL winner. The team has been furnished with everything it needs to stay that way: A new £10m training facility, an inspirational manager with aspirational targets, an influx of WSL-ready talent. And of course they have Bunny Shaw. The PFA player of the year is already off to a flyer.

In a Women's Super League season where consistency has already hampered their biggest rivals, City's will to win appears more resolute than ever. They do not intend to be a one hit wonder. They have worked too hard to just be considered winners. They want to qualify as champions.

articles.title: Walker 'desperate' to end Burnley's winless woe
articles.summary: Burnley defender Kyle Walker says he has "never wanted a victory as much" as against Derby County on Saturday, as Clarets aim to turn around their sorry star...
articles.body:
Burnley defender Kyle Walker said he has "never wanted a victory as much" as against Derby County on Saturday, as Clarets aim to turn around their sorry start to the season.

Bottom of the Championship and without a victory inside 90 minutes this term , Burnley's winless run stretches back to 11 February and 22 games - including a run of 13 games at the tail end of a 2025-26 campaign where they were relegated from the Premier League.

Walker, who won 17 trophies with Manchester City prior to his move to Turf Moor in July 2025 and was part of City's Treble-winning squad in 2023, has played in six Championship games so far this term.

"I'm desperate," he told BBC Radio Lancashire. "I've never wanted a victory so much because there's a lot of noise.

"Am I the most talented player? Definitely not. I played with many more talented players than me but what I pride myself on is working hard and proving people wrong.

"That's what hopefully I can prove by coming out and being the voice of the of the players and hopefully they're listening to this and they take this on board that I'm not laying down and I'm willing to fight for the all the way to the very end."

Prior to joining Burnley, Walker had been regarded as one of the best right-backs in world football and had enjoyed an enormous amount of success at Manchester City under the stewardship of Pep Guardiola.

The relationship between Walker and Guardiola broke down , leading to him spending time on loan with Italian giants AC Milan , but the England international returned to England with Burnley ahead of what had been their return to the Premier League last year.

Asked about how the difference between winning regularly with City to the contrast of the past 14 months with Burnley, Walker said it had been a tough transition.

"I've probably not experienced this ever. It's a different dressing room to what I was in at City where everyone kind of marshalled themselves," he added

"You didn't have to really rile people up to get them a game of football out of them. They had their own standards and they set their own bars to then go and achieve certain things.

"I think that's why they're at Manchester City and why Manchester City were so successful because we had a great manager.

"I think even if Pep wasn't there we would have gone on and achieved a lot of things as well because we had a great team and a great togetherness within that.

"I'm not saying that the togetherness is not within Burnley because it completely is, it's a great bunch of lads."

Saturday's fixture against Derby (15:00 BST) is the final game before the new, extended September and October international break and will be the last match they play for three weeks.

Walker is torn on how to view the break, whether it provides an opportunity to push on in October should they win at the weekend or if it is a welcome period of respite after a tough start to the campaign.

"I think you can look at it in two ways. You win on Saturday and you want to keep going then, don't you?" he said.

"You're losing, you're kind of thinking, thank God the international break's coming, you can kind of go back to the drawing board and start again.

"It's a bit weird for me because I've never experienced this in my career where I'm saying that I want this international break to come, good or bad.

"But it's the position that we're in and we're not here to beat around the bush, we're here to talk face to face and man up on it and we need a win, that's the be all and end all of it."
